item.title: Siena's league adding Stonehill College for 2027-28 season
item.description: The Metro Conference is adding Stonehill. (Metro Conference) The Metro Conference keeps getting bigger at the Northeast Conference's expense. The Metro, which includes Siena University, announced Friday the addition of Stonehill College, effective July 1, 2027, to bring the league's membership to a record 14 schools for the 2027-28 season. Stonehill, located in North Easton, Mass., is the second NEC school in three weeks to accept an invitation from the Metro. Le Moyne College in Syracuse is also joining the Metro in 2027-28 . Mount St. Mary's, Merrimack and Sacred Heart have also departed the NEC for the Metro since 2022. "We are excited to welcome Stonehill College as the 14th member of the Metro Conference," said Metro commissioner Travis Tellitocci said in a news release. "With an outstanding campus, the excitement surrounding the development of Bogan Arena, and a clear vision for the future, Stonehill has demonstrated a strong commitment to investing in its Division I athletics program and is an institution on the rise. Our Council of Presidents has been intentional in identifying institutions that are committed to investing in athletics and positioning themselves for long-term success." Fairfield is leaving the Metro for the Coastal Athletic Association after this academic year. Stonehill began its reclassification from Division II to Division I in July 22 and completed an accelerated transition on July 1, 2025. The Skyhawks became full NCAA Division I active members for the 2025-26 academic year. Stonehill previously belonged to the Division II Northeast 10 Conference, where the Skyhawks were rivals of The College of Saint Rose, which closed in 2024. Last May, Stonehill announced a planned $50 million improvement of its athletic facilties, including a new basketball and hockey arena. Stonehill said it had $22.5 million in commitments. Stonehill is a Division I independent in hockey. Last season, Stonehill men's basketball went 12-21 and the women's team was 12-18. The teams currently play in Merkert Gymnasium, with a capacity of 1,560. Siena president Chuck Seifert, who is chair of the Metro Council of Presidents, said "Stonehill embodies everything the Metro stands for" because of its academic excellence, strong faith-based values and commitment to investing in Division I athletics. "At a time of significant shift throughout the NCAA, this move underscores our league's determination to be proactive and bold in shaping our own trajectory," Seifert said. "Reaching a record 14 member institutions and strengthening our New England footprint enhances our competitive landscape." Frank Ambrose, who is Siena's advisor to athletic director John D'Argenio for revenue sharing and NIL strategy, was less enthusiastic about adding another team from the NEC, historically one of the lowest-rated conferences in Division I basketball. Ambrose questioned how it would strengthen men's basketball and keep the Metro champion from needing to play in the NCAA To

Fairfield is leaving the Metro for the Coastal Athletic Association after this academic year. Last May, Stonehill announced a planned $50 million improvement of its athletic facilties, including a new basketball and hockey arena. Stonehill said it had $22.5 million in commitments. Stonehill is a Division I independent in hockey. Last season, Stonehill men's basketball went 12-21 and the women's team was 12-18. The teams currently play in Merkert Gymnasium, with a capacity of 1,560. Siena president Chuck Seifert, who is chair of the Metro Council of Presidents, said "Stonehill embodies everything the Metro stands for" because of its academic excellence, strong faith-based values and commitment to investing in Division I athletics. "At a time of significant shift throughout the NCAA, this move underscores our league's determination to be proactive and bold in shaping our own trajectory," Seifert said. "Reaching a record 14 member institutions and strengthening our New England footprint enhances our competitive landscape." Frank Ambrose, who is Siena's advisor to athletic director John D'Argenio for revenue sharing and NIL strategy, was less enthusiastic about adding another team from the NEC, historically one of the lowest-rated conferences in Division I basketball. Ambrose questioned how it would strengthen men's basketball and keep the Metro champion from needing to play in the NCAA Tournament's opening round, which will be played in Dayton, Ohio, and Wichita, Kan. with the tournament's expansion to 76 teams. "I'm sorry I just don't see this as a net plus but the conference has been playing defense for years and our NET rating shows that," Ambrose posted on X. "Maybe @StonehillMBB will be a Merrimack add but what is the @MetroConfSports actual plan continuing to reach into the @NEC, locking us into a trip to Dayton???" Mount St. Mary's men's basketball won the Metro championship in 2025. Merrimack won the regular-season title by three games last season before losing to Siena in the championship game in Atlantic City. Siena has belonged to the Metro since the 1989-90 season. With Fairfield's departure, Iona, Manhattan and Saint Peter's are the remaining charter members from the league's first season in 1981-82. Subscribe There’s more to Albany with the Times Union. item.title: OSU's Legree leads nation in receiving as WSU clash looms
item.description: CORVALLIS — There may be no more appropriate way to describe Oregon State’s outrageously successful passing game this season than explosive. The Beavers lead the country in passing yards thanks in large part to 10 passes of 40-plus yards. Jesse Legree is responsible for eight of those catches, including all five of OSU’s 50-yard pass plays this season, making it no surprise that he leads the country in receiving yards and touchdowns entering this week’s matchup with Washington State. “You see him with ball in space, obviously taking the top off a number of times,” Washington State coach Kirby Moore said. “I think it’s about playing team defense. Obviously communication is going to be really important, where he’s at.” The Cougars (1-5, 0-2 Pac-12) have the No. 2 defense in the Pac-12 thus far and are having that success by keeping the top on their pass coverage. WSU has allowed 11 passes of 30-plus yards, which is tied for 129th nationally and nearly 10% of the passes it has allowed. However, opponents are not breaking through that mark often, with just four passes over 40 yards and none for more than 50, one of 30 teams yet to allow such a play this season. “We don’t want to let the verticals up,” Washington State safety Jaylen Smith said. “We take pride in (not) letting deep balls go. We always look to play top down and take away the deep routes first.” WSU defensive coordinator Trent Bray will be tasked with doing what nobody has been able to do yet this season: contain Legree. OSU offensive coordinator Mitch Dahlen has been creative in moving Legree around to prevent defenses from taking him away. Last week against San Diego State that included moving Legree into the backfield for a variety of plays. “People are going to try and hit him at the line of scrimmage,” Dahlen said. “They’re going to try and two-hand jam. If they’re going to try and two-hand jam, it’s like OK, how can I move this guy enough where you can’t do that? You put him in the backfield, unless you want to jump offsides and do it, you can’t do it that way. “That’s what we do a good job of as a staff, is moving him around where you can’t just put a safety over the top of him because if he’s in the backfield, what are you going to do there?” Even if the Cougars manage to limit Legree, the Beavers have shown they are more than capable of going elsewhere, with an outrageous 14 players catching passes last week. Aeryn Hampton (20 receptions for 245 yards) and tight ends Eric Olsen and DeCorion Temple each have at least 20 catches and Aaron Butler has four grabs for at least 20 yards. They’re confident they can challenge any defense vertically. “The underneath throws are going to be there,” Hampton said. “We got the best OC in the country; we’re going to be able to go deep if we want to.” Latest Beavers news Scouting the Broncos: 5 questions, prediction with a Boise State reporter Oregon State QB Braden Atkinson going through further testing of hand injury before Boise State game Or

item.title: Are De’Aaron Fox, Devin Vassell playing tonight? Spurs vs. Warriors injury report
item.description: Credit: Troy Wayrynen-Imagn Images Are De’Aaron Fox, Devin Vassell playing tonight? Spurs vs. Warriors injury report appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The San Antonio Spurs could be without two key contributors for Friday night’s NBA Cup matchup against the Golden State Warriors , as guards De’Aaron Fox and Devin Vassell received injury updates. San Antonio’s latest injury report lists Fox as questionable with left hip soreness and Vassell as questionable with left adductor tightness. The Spurs (10-2) will host the Warriors (8-4) at 9:30 p.m. ET on Prime Video, looking to extend their winning streak to 11 games after overcoming an 0-2 start. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Both players’ availability remains uncertain ahead of the contest, with San Antonio attempting to maintain its early-season momentum. Fox last appeared in San Antonio’s 124-119 victory over the Chicago Bulls on Wednesday, finishing with 17 points, nine assists, four rebounds and three steals in 31 minutes. The veteran guard shot 7-for-17 from the field and 2-for-7 from 3-point range, helping San Antonio complete a four-game road trip undefeated. Meanwhile, Vassell missed Wednesday’s victory because of his adductor injury, marking his second consecutive absence. His questionable designation leaves open the possibility of returning against Golden State. Fox is averaging 14.2 points, 6.2 assists and 4.3 rebounds through 12 games this season while shooting 51.4% from the field. Vassell has averaged 11.9 points, 3.8 rebounds and 3.1 assists through 10 appearances, shooting 35.6% from beyond the arc. The 26-year-old last appeared in San Antonio’s 125-103 victory over the Portland Trail Blazers on Nov. 7, recording 15 points, three assists, two rebounds and two steals in 21 minutes. Spurs, Warriors dealing with injuries ahead of NBA Cup clash Scott Wachter-Imagn Images San Antonio’s injury report also lists veteran forward Tobias Harris as out with a left calf strain and rookie Jayden Quaintance as out following right knee surgery. Meanwhile, Golden State will be without Stephen Curry, who suffered a right oblique tear during Wednesday’s 115-108 loss to the Houston Rockets and is expected to miss at least two weeks. The Warriors’ injury report also lists Jimmy Butler III, Moses Moody, and Brandon Williams as out. Despite their injury concerns, the Spurs enter Friday’s matchup riding a 10-game winning streak, with their latest victory featuring 32 points, nine rebounds and five blocks from Victor Wembanyama. San Antonio will look to maintain its momentum against a Golden State team attempting to rebound from Wednesday’s loss without its star guard. Related: Spurs’ De’Aaron Fox, Devin Vassell get big injury updates for Warriors clash Related: Charles Barkley pinpoints Spurs as NBA title favorites after Thunder’s injury bug

item.title: Tearful Pochettino says leaving USA for Manchester United ‘most difficult decision’ of career: football – live
item.description: Pochettino speaks in emotional press conference Today’s fixtures | Follow us on TikTok | Mail Dominic Barney Ronay was at Wembley on Thursday night to celebrate Happy Harry Kane day. “And as the teams lined up there was a surprise appearance from the real star of this stage, the Ballon d’Or itself, wreathed in event glamour and star-flash. Kane drew the ballon from its stone in Arthurian fashion, then held it a little sheepishly in one hand. Prince William walked out and gave him a massive framed shirt, which seemed weird in the moment, like the chief area sales manager presenting the prize from the Christmas raffle. Has Prince William ever been asked to carry anything before?” Continue reading...

item.title: Hutton among trio to sign new Notts deals
item.description: Brett Hutton made his first-class debut for Nottinghamshire in 2011 [Shutterstock] Nottinghamshire seam bowler Brett Hutton is among a trio of players to sign new deals with the County Championship side. The 33-year-old, who was the club's leading wicket-taker with 38 when they won the Division One title in 2025, has agreed to remain at Trent Bridge until the end of the 2028 campaign. Hutton has spent 13 seasons with Nottinghamshire across two spells and has taken 357 wickets across all formats for them. Fellow seam bowler Tom Giles, 20, and 23-year-old all-rounder Ben Martindale have also extended their stays with the club, having both come though the academy as Hutton did more than a decade earlier. "I always want to keep making a difference for us in every facet of the game, and having been around the club for a while now, I also want to help the younger players coming through," Hutton told the club's website. "I've got the same hunger to perform and help this team achieve success that I've always had, and there's a great feeling among the strong group that we've got here at the moment." Giles, who has signed a new two-year deal, made his first-class debut for the club last season and went on to take five wickets in four County Championship appearances. Martindale, whose father Duncan also played for Nottinghamshire, has featured 32 times across all formats and has been a regular in the club's second XI side for a number of years. His new deal keeps him at Trent Bridge for a further 12 months.

item.title: Jalen Green Trade Rumors Heat Up As Suns Reportedly Seek Proven Point Guard
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Jalen Green scored 12 points against the Charlotte Hornets on Thursday, then watched the entire fourth quarter from the bench as Devin Booker closed out a 101–96 Phoenix Suns win. One rotation decision won’t determine Green’s future, but it captured how much his role has changed. The Suns once insisted Houston Rockets include him in the Kevin Durant trade. Now rival teams are wondering whether Phoenix would move him for a point guard. According to Sam Amick of The Athletic , the belief around the league is that the Suns are motivated to swap Green for a proven floor general. A Phoenix source gave Amick a more measured account: The front office intends to give this roster time and may wait until later in the season before seriously engaging in trade talks. “When Phoenix owner Mat Ishbia approved the Kevin Durant trade with Houston in the summer of 2025, it was because the Rockets had finally relented on the players that the Suns coveted. And Jalen Green, the No. 2 pick in the 2021 draft who was entering his fifth season at the time, was seen internally as a must-have part of the package.” “‘It was never gonna get done without Jalen and Dillon (Brooks) in the deal,’ Ishbia told me earlier this year. ‘Those are the two players we wanted. It wasn’t, ‘Hey, how do we fill a salary with these numbers?’ It was, ‘In order to have Kevin Durant on your team, I want Dillon Brooks to help me with my culture and my identity. I want Jalen Green as a 23-year-old up-and-coming leading scorer.’” “They landed Green, of course, but that last part about him heading up their offensive efforts has simply not come to bear for these Suns (5-6). After averaging 21 points per game in his final Rockets season, Green’s scoring dipped to 17.8 in his first season with the Suns (in just 32 games) and currently stands at just 11.8 through his first 10 games (he’s fourth in scoring behind Devin Booker, Miles Bridges and Brooks). In turn, there is a great deal of interest around the league in how Phoenix will handle Green (who has a player option worth $36 million for next season) heading into the deadline.” “The outside belief is that they are motivated to swap Green for a proven point guard. The Suns, according to a team source, insist that they’ll remain patient with their roster and don’t plan to truly engage in trade talks, potentially, until later in the season.” That’s a notable shift from the summer of 2025, when owner Mat Ishbia saw Green as a player worth holding up the Durant deal for. item.content:encoded: Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Jalen Green scored 12 points against the Charlotte Hornets on Thursday, then watched the entire fourth quarter from the bench as Devin Booker closed out a 101–96 Phoenix Suns win. One rotation decision won’t determine Green’s future, but it captured how much his role has changed. The Suns once insisted Houston Rockets include him in the Kevin Durant trade. Now rival teams are wondering whether Phoenix would move him for a point guard. According to Sam Amick of The Athletic , the belief around the league is that the Suns are motivated to swap Green for a proven floor general. A Phoenix source gave Amick a more measured account: The front office intends to give this roster time and may wait until later in the season before seriously engaging in trade talks. “When Phoenix owner Mat Ishbia approved the Kevin Durant trade with Houston in the summer of 2025, it was because the Rockets had finally relented on the players that the Suns coveted. And Jalen Green, the No. 2 pick in the 2021 draft who was entering his fifth season at the time, was seen internally as a must-have part of the package.” “‘It was never gonna get done without Jalen and Dillon (Brooks) in the deal,’ Ishbia told me earlier this year. ‘Those are the two players we wanted. It wasn’t, ‘Hey, how do we fill a salary with these numbers?’ It was, ‘In order to have Kevin Durant on your team, I want Dillon Brooks to help me with my culture and my identity. I want Jalen Green as a 23-year-old up-and-coming leading scorer.’” “They landed Green, of course, but that last part about him heading up their offensive efforts has simply not come to bear for these Suns (5-6). After averaging 21 points per game in his final Rockets season, Green’s scoring dipped to 17.8 in his first season with the Suns (in just 32 games) and currently stands at just 11.8 through his first 10 games (he’s fourth in scoring behind Devin Booker, Miles Bridges and Brooks). In turn, there is a great deal of interest around the league in how Phoenix will handle Green (who has a player option worth $36 million for next season) heading into the deadline.” “The outside belief is that they are motivated to swap Green for a proven point guard. The Suns, according to a team source, insist that they’ll remain patient with their roster and don’t plan to truly engage in trade talks, potentially, until later in the season.” That’s a notable shift from the summer of 2025, when owner Mat Ishbia saw Green as a player worth holding up the Durant deal for. Phoenix wanted Dillon Brooks to help establish its identity and Green to give it another young scorer capable of carrying an offense. The Suns got both, along with the draft rights to Khaman Maluach and five second-round picks. Green averaged 21.0 points in his final season with Houston and 17.8 in his first year with Phoenix, when a hamstring injury limited him to 32 games. He’s down to 11.8 points through 10 appearances this season, fourth on the team behind Devin Booker, Miles Bridges , and Dillon Brooks . He’s also averaging 3.4 assists, and his $36 million player option for 2027–28 gives Phoenix another decision to weigh as the deadline approaches. Chris Haynes reported in October that some Suns players were already frustrated by the lack of a traditional point guard. Booker can run the offense, but there’s a difference between asking him to create an advantage against a set defense and getting him the ball after a teammate has already forced a rotation. An experienced lead guard could give Booker more catches on the move and get players like Maluach easier looks at the rim. Dejounte Murray is one example of the kind of player who could help. Bleacher Report’s Dan Favale floated a deal centered on Green and Murray , though that was a trade proposal rather than a report of negotiations. Murray’s pick-and-roll passing addresses a clear need. His perimeter shooting and Achilles injury history also show why the Suns should be selective about what they give up for a veteran. In the meantime, Jordan Ott can give Collin Gillespie more possessions alongside Booker and see how the offense looks with a dedicated organizer. Gillespie scored 13 points and hit three threes against Charlotte, a reminder that Phoenix has an internal option worth testing. Green is still 24, and moving him while his scoring is down could mean selling low. If the Suns do trade him, the return should be someone they trust to run the offense in the fourth quarter, when Booker needs help most.

item.title: Fantasy Football Week 10 Start 'Em Sit 'Em: Tucker Kraft or Kyle Pitts?
item.description: Nov 8, 2026; Madrid, ESP; Atlanta Falcons tight end Kyle Pitts Sr. (8) reacts after making a reception against the Cincinnati Bengals during the second quarter at Bernabeu Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Fantasy managers entered 2026 with high hopes for Tucker Kraft and Kyle Pitts. Each had the potential to be the top at their position, but they've mostly fallen short. They currently meet the criteria for being weekly tight end start-sit debates. That is where I will come in. Using historical findings of what proves accurate and inaccurate for start-sit debates, the following data projects who to trust in Week 10. The Case of Tucker Kraft I find volume and usage paramount. If both are proven over time, they avoid being a floor player; instead, when they do score a touchdown, it significantly raises the player's floor and ceiling. Kraft has played nine games this season. Over that span, he is averaging 5.7 targets, 4.0 receptions, and 39.0 yards per game. Kraft has a 19.8% targets-per-route run rate and a 74% Route Rate. How good has Kraft truly been as a football player? That is a measure I value when evaluating a player. Kraft ranks 24th at his position in PFF Receiving Grade and 10th in EPA per Target. In 2025, Kraft was among the most explosive tight ends in football, but this year he averages merely 9.8 Yards per reception, which is quite average. item.title: England fly-half Harrison signs new Saracens deal
item.description: Zoe Harrison helped Saracens win this year's Premiership Women's Rugby title [Shutterstock] England fly-half Zoe Harrison has renewed her contract with Saracens for the forthcoming Premiership Women's Rugby campaign. The 28-year-old has spent her entire professional career with the London side and started every game for England at last year's World Cup. She went on to help Saracens win last season's PWR title as the league's leading points scorer, as well as being part of the England side that won the Six Nations in the spring. "Zoe has established herself as one of the premier 10s in world rugby," Saracens director of rugby Alex Austerberry told the club website. "Having represented the club well over 100 times and represented the Red Roses over 70 times she has great experience and this is invaluable when it comes to on-field and off-field management."

item.title: ‘The most comparable to Tom Brady’: Maxx Crosby says Joe Burrow is ‘the closest person we’ve seen’ to Tom Brady
item.description: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Over the past several years, Cincinnati Bengals superstar quarterback Joe Burrow has emerged as one of the top quarterbacks in the league. But longtime veteran star pass rusher Maxx Crosby wants everyone to know just how good he truly is. During a recent interview, Crosby said that if you “know ball,” you truly understand just how good Burrow is, as he went as far as to compare him to Tom Brady. Burrow’s Big Season Burrow and the Bengals are rolling right now. Cincinnati beat the Atlanta Falcons 34-17 in Madrid last week to improve to 6-2, extending its winning streak to four games. Burrow completed 24 of 29 passes for 271 yards, three touchdowns, and no interceptions in the win, while also running in a touchdown. Ja’Marr Chase had 10 catches for 155 yards and a score, and Tee Higgins caught two touchdowns. Burrow’s 21 passing touchdowns lead the NFL. He also leads the league in completion percentage and is second in the league in passing yards, behind only Jordan Love. And he has been getting plenty of love lately. Earlier this week, ESPN’s Louis Riddick said on The Dan Patrick Show that Burrow is “that guy” and that there’s no other quarterback he would take over him. ‘The most comparable to Tom Brady’ Crosby discussed Burrow and Chase on the latest episode of his podcast, The Rush with Maxx Crosby . He made it clear he has been a Burrow believer for a long time. “He’s one of the best quarterbacks in the league. I’ve been saying that since, you know, since day one,” Crosby said. Then Crosby took it a step further. “So, yeah, if you know ball, you realize how good Joe Burrow is. He’s the most comparable, in my opinion. This is, and obviously there’s still levels and all that, but he’s the most comparable to Tom Brady in the way he plays in my eyes. I think he’s the closest person we’ve seen in that regard. Now, you got to go get seven of them, you know, to really be in that world. I’m sure of it, you know, but yeah, just the way he plays, the way he operates, and his pocket presence, I think, is the best thing about his game,” Crosby said. Crosby did have one piece of advice for Burrow, who has dealt with several injuries during his career. “Now, he takes some unnecessary blows. Even if you put a flag, even if he’s playing flag football, for some reason, Joe Burrow loves to take the worst spills of all time. If somebody can just get in there with [him] maybe and figure out how to land a little, like, more gracefully, I think would maybe do wonders for him,” Crosby continued. That’s high praise coming from one of the best pass rushers in the league. The post ‘The most comparable to Tom Brady’: Maxx Crosby says Joe Burrow is ‘the closest person we’ve seen’ to Tom Brady appeared first on The Comeback: Today’s Top Sports Stories & Reactions .

item.title: Al Michaels Gets Choked Up During Tribute to Late Broadcaster Dan Hicks on “Thursday Night Football”
item.description: Al Michaels, Dan Hicks Credit: Kevin Mazur/Getty; Tim Bradbury/Getty NEED TO KNOW Al Michaels got emotional in a tribute to Dan Hicks Hicks, 64, died after an acute illness, his wife Hannah Storm announced on Thursday, Nov. 12 Hicks worked for NBC for 34 years, covering golf and Olympic events including swimming and alpine skiing Al Michaels shared an emotional tribute to Dan Hicks during Thursday Night Football . The broadcaster took a moment to honor the NBC sportscaster, whose death at the age of 64 was announced on Thursday, Nov. 12 by his wife Hannah Storm . “All of us in the sports broadcasting business were shocked to learn this morning of the passing of Dan Hicks,” Michaels, 82, said. “Dan joined NBC Sports in 1992, provided captions to so many iconic moments in golf, tennis and Notre Dame football, and he and Rowdy Gaines turned the calling of swimming at multiple Olympics into an art form.” Michaels continued, his voice breaking, “He was genial. He was compassionate. Great company. Had a world-class sense of humor. And on this very rough day for so many of us, we send our love to Hannah [Storm] and your three daughters. Wishing you strength and comfort.” Hannah Storm and husband Dan Hicks at the Breast Cancer Research Foundation’s Hot Pink Party in May 2025. Credit: Santiago Felipe/Getty Hicks died “following an acute illness,” Storm shared in a social media post early on Thursday. “He was a devoted husband of over 30 years, loving father to our three daughters, and cherished friend to so many,” the ESPN broadcaster, 64, wrote. “His loss is immeasurable.” Storm continued: “Dan was truly one of a kind and, quite simply, the person everyone wanted to be around. When he walked into a room, he brought the energy, the laughter and the people together. He was endlessly kind, thoughtful and funny, and he made everyone feel like they mattered.” Hicks — who maintained a busy work schedule yet made time to root on one of his daughters in the Chicago Marathon last month before his unexpected death — was set to call this weekend’s Notre Dame game, something he had done for seven seasons. Jason Benetti, NBC’s Sunday Night Baseball play-by-play voice, will step in alongside analyst Jason Garrett for the game against Boston College on Saturday, Nov. 14. Among the many who shared tributes to Hicks on Thursday was swimmer Michael Phelps . The late broadcaster called all 28 of Phelps’ Olympic medal-winning races from 2004 through 2016, according to NBC Sports . Follow your favorite athletes on and off the field with PEOPLE’s free sports newsletter — sign up now! “This one hurts,” Phelps, 41, wrote on Instagram . “Really don’t even know what to say right now. There are certain voices in sports that you hear and instantly know who it is…. Dan had one of those voices. A voice that so many of us grew up listening to, a voice that brought some of the biggest moments in sports to life…. And for me, a voice that will forever be part of my story. But he was so m

item.title: Patriots takeaways from Germany: What Mike Vrabel said about A.J. Brown playing in Munich
item.description: MUNICH – After making the trip to Munich, will A.J. Brown play on Sunday against the Detroit Lions? That was the big question facing the Patriots on Friday. Temperatures dipped into the low 40s as the team held a full 90-minute practice at the FC Bayern Munich training facility. After flying into Munich on Thursday, and holding a 60-minute walkthrough, Mike Vrabel’s team picked up the pace. The Patriots coach said he felt “pretty good” about the status of A.J. Brown and Rhamondre Stevenson after watching the two players at Thursday’s practice. “So, let’s go through today and see where that goes and then meet with (trainer) Jim (Whalen) and meet with players,” Vrabel said. Brown has played in three of nine games this season. The Pro Bowl receiver missed four weeks in a row after suffering a high ankle sprain in the team’s regular-season opener in Seattle. After returning, and playing twice in five days, Brown’s been dealing with a nagging knee injury. The receiver missed two weeks of practices and the Patriots matchups against Miami and Green Bay. Brown returned to practice on Wednesday before flying with the team on Thursday. “I think the more that we can get everybody back, I think the more that it contributes to what we feel like we want to be as a team,” Vrabel said when asked about having Brown at practice. “And one guy certainly doesn’t make the difference, but it’s certainly the more that we can get guys back. It’s exciting that the pieces can start to build and come together. So, you know, we’ll see where things go today. And hopefully, you know, those guys that haven’t been with us or maybe got hurt last week, that could be available.” In three games, Brown’s caught nine passes for 101 yards. He’d be a huge boost for Drake Maye and the offense, if healthy. After dealing with two different injuries, Vrabel was asked if the team needed to protect Brown from himself when it comes to how much they play him when he does return. item.content:encoded: MUNICH – After making the trip to Munich, will A.J. Brown play on Sunday against the Detroit Lions? That was the big question facing the Patriots on Friday. Temperatures dipped into the low 40s as the team held a full 90-minute practice at the FC Bayern Munich training facility. After flying into Munich on Thursday, and holding a 60-minute walkthrough, Mike Vrabel’s team picked up the pace. The Patriots coach said he felt “pretty good” about the status of A.J. Brown and Rhamondre Stevenson after watching the two players at Thursday’s practice. “So, let’s go through today and see where that goes and then meet with (trainer) Jim (Whalen) and meet with players,” Vrabel said. Brown has played in three of nine games this season. The Pro Bowl receiver missed four weeks in a row after suffering a high ankle sprain in the team’s regular-season opener in Seattle. After returning, and playing twice in five days, Brown’s been dealing with a nagging knee injury. The receiver missed two weeks of practices and the Patriots matchups against Miami and Green Bay. Brown returned to practice on Wednesday before flying with the team on Thursday. “I think the more that we can get everybody back, I think the more that it contributes to what we feel like we want to be as a team,” Vrabel said when asked about having Brown at practice. “And one guy certainly doesn’t make the difference, but it’s certainly the more that we can get guys back. It’s exciting that the pieces can start to build and come together. So, you know, we’ll see where things go today. And hopefully, you know, those guys that haven’t been with us or maybe got hurt last week, that could be available.” In three games, Brown’s caught nine passes for 101 yards. He’d be a huge boost for Drake Maye and the offense, if healthy. After dealing with two different injuries, Vrabel was asked if the team needed to protect Brown from himself when it comes to how much they play him when he does return. RELATED: Early data projections: Pats head to Germany seeking a huge rebound in Week 10 vs. Lions “I mean, again, we just have to try to see where things go and how they feel, and we got to trust them a little bit, how they tell us and also have a plan for each and every guy,” Vrabel said. “I think it’s kind of see how it goes.” In their final injury report, Brown was ruled questionable for Sunday’s game against Detroit. Here are the top takeaways from the Patriots’ second day in Munich: Will Rhamondre Stevenson play? If Brown plays, it’d be a huge boost for the offense. The same can be said if Rhamondre Stevenson is cleared to play on Sunday. The running back suffered a knee injury last weekend against Green Bay. On Monday, ESPN and the NFL Network reported Stevenson would miss weeks due to his injury. However, Stevenson flew with the team to Munich and practiced the last two days. Stevenson’s presence here has been surprising. Vrabel said the veteran is working hard to play and admires his attitude. “I think we’re just always looking for guys that are looking for ways in as opposed to ways out,” Vrabel said. “At this point in the season, 10 weeks straight without a bye, there’s pretty much nobody out there that’s 100% and we have to realize that. We have to recognize that. But we also have to find ways to do our job and Rhamondre’s one of those players that is looking for a way in.” Stevenson was with his teammates at the start of practice, but was not wearing his jersey. The team listed him as limited on Thursday. Considering he’s the Patriots leading rusher and his impact in the passing game within blitz pickup, it’d be huge for the offense if Stevenson could play this weekend. The running back was listed as questionable in the team’s final injury report. TreVeyon Henderson update The Patriots running back room is running short. TreVeyon Henderson didn’t travel with the team this week due to his illness. Last week, Henderson revealed that he’d been dealing with an undiagnosed neurological condition. Vrabel said he didn’t have a timeline for the speedy back’s return. “I talk to TreVeyon every day and just like everybody else that’s not available, he’s working hard to get back and when that is, I don’t know,” Vrabel said. “I don’t have a timetable. But I love my interactions with him, I love talking with him.” If Henderson is going to be out for the foreseeable future, the Patriots could place him on the non-football injury list. The issue, however, is that the team is running out of injured reserve-return slots. Every team gets eight per season. The Patriots already used five with Romeo Doubs and Alijah Vera-Tucker eligible to return after the bye week. Vrabel was asked if they’re weighing putting Henderson on the reserve list due to the limited options they have. “Yeah, those are things that we work through. You know, we’re very conscious of that and we’re just until we absolutely need the spot and we haven’t had that necessarily pinch and still also just have to try to figure out when he may be available,” Vrabel said. “But then also you’re right, we have guys coming back from, from injured reserve or designated to return. So there’s a lot of things that we have to weigh through with the roster.” Why Patriots arrived early The Patriots lost their last two international matchups in London and Frankfurt. In both cases, the Patriots flew Thursday night and held one practice on Friday before the Sunday matchup. This week, Vrabel opted to change that by having the team fly in a day early to get two practices in to help ease the jetlag. “You know, just having done this a few times and maybe how you feel coming over here on Friday and what you’re able to get done. I felt like we wanted to try to do a little bit more maybe than had been done in the past on a Friday,” Vrabel said. “So, get here a day early to be able to walk through. Come over here last night, walk through. I thought helped guys just get moving a little bit, get the airplane and get the flight out of us and then got up this morning. It’s been a regular Friday and we’ll get going on practice here pretty soon.” Homecoming for Patriots tackle This week has been a homecoming for Lorenz Metz . The Patriots offensive tackle was born in Neuötting in Bavaria, Germany. Metz has had an interesting journey to the NFL as he didn’t play football until 18. Now, he’s close to his hometown and practicing at the training facility for the soccer team he grew up rooting for. “It’s a surreal feeling,” Metz said. “I grew up about an hour from here. FC Bayern was the team for me—Thomas Müller, (Manuel) Neuer, all those Bayern players were my idols. To be standing on this pitch now—it’s just incredible.” Metz played in the German Football League for the Kirchdorf Wildcats in 2017. The next year, he moved to the United States and played collegiately at Cincinnati. In 2023, he entered the NFL as an undrafted free agent. He’s been on the practice squads in Chicago and Tampa Bay before joining the Patriots practice squad last season. Metz said he started to watch the NFL when Germany first started broadcasting the games. At the time, the Patriots and Tom Brady were the most popular. “I think it was around 2012 when they started broadcasting regular-season games on free-to-air TV in Germany,” Metz said. “Back then—2012, 2014, 2016—the Patriots were right at the top, thanks to Tom Brady. They were the team everyone knew; everyone knew Tom Brady.” This week, Metz gathered his teammates for a team dinner in Munich. He wouldn’t reveal what restaurant they went to, but said he wanted to give Patriots teammates a true feel of the food and culture that he grew up in. “I wanted to give my teammates a taste of Bavarian culture,” Metz said. “We’ll definitely have some beer steins, and there will be traditional Bavarian dishes like roast pork and schnitzel.” Milton Williams institutes $1,000 fine Milton Williams has seen enough. item.title: Here's How Much Steelers vs. Bengals Means for Playoff Positioning, Division Race
item.description: Here's How Much Steelers vs. Bengals Means for Playoff Positioning, Division Race originally appeared on SportsNet Pittsburgh . Add SportsNet Pittsburgh as a Preferred Source by clicking here . When the Steelers travel to play the Bengals on Sunday night, it marks the biggest game of the season so far for Pittsburgh. Both the Steelers and Bengals are 6-2 entering the game, with Pittsburgh ahead in the standings thanks to a win over Cincinnati earlier this season. As a result, the winner of this game will take the spot atop the AFC North standings, which would mean owning one of the top four seeds in AFC playoff positioning. Even with that in play, the game means much more than just a temporary first-place spot. Whoever wins this game will increase their odds to make the playoffs and win the AFC North by a significant margin while also delivering a blow to the loser's chances at winning the division and earning a postseason spot. Here's a breakdown of how much this game means for the Steelers. Steelers vs. Bengals playoff odds The Steelers' game this weekend against the Bengals on Sunday night is Pittsburgh's biggest game of the season, as proven by the team's playoff odds. A win would give the Steelers an inside track towards winning the division, while a loss would drop them to a wild-card spot. Current playoff probability: 79% Playoff probability with win: 89% (+10%) Playoff probability with loss: 72% (-7%) A win by the Steelers would improve their chances of making the playoffs by 10 percent, according to NFL.com , while a loss would drop their chances by 7 percent. item.title: Three call-ups, three goals: This is what Devils depth looks like
item.description: Three players came up from Utica. All three scored. One tied the game, one won it and one gave the Devils enough breathing room to exhale. That’s a pretty good night for the guys who weren’t in the lineup the last time the Devils played. Lenni Hämeenaho, Vladislav Kolyachonok and Stefan Noesen all scored in Thursday’s 5–2 win over the Capitals at Prudential Center. Connor Hellebuyck made 26 saves to improve to 6-0-0, a franchise record. For Saturday’s rematch between the Devils and the Capitals, the over/under is set at 6.5 total goals on Kalshi . Also, view our in-depth guide to the best sportsbook promos to shop for the most competitive odds. Brenden Dillon played what Sheldon Keefe thought might have been his best game of the season, and the Devils did all of it on a night when their coach flat-out said they weren’t at their best. That’s the part that should get your attention. The schedule has been a grind, bodies are coming out of the lineup and the Devils are still finding different guys to win them hockey games. ‘Utica hat trick’ “It’s a Utica hat trick,” Keefe said. Hämeenaho got the first one. The Devils were down 2–1 in the second when Dillon put a puck toward the net and it went in off Hämeenaho’s glove. He showed the mark it left in the locker room afterward. Lenni Hameenaho shows where Brenden Dillon's shot hit his glove before going in Anthony Corona “It wasn’t a pretty one, but I’ll take that every day of the week,” Hämeenaho said. Then came Kolyachonok, playing his third game in three nights and his first as a Devil. By the third period, he’d put a puck on net from the blue line that found its way in for the winner. And then Noesen looked like he got shot out of a cannon. He raced to a loose puck and roofed a backhander to make it 4–2. Jack Hughes added the empty-netter. General manager Sunny Mehta has been preaching depth since he got to New Jersey. “Optionality” is a big deal to him at every level of the organization, and this is what it looks like. Brenden Dillon needs to be in the lineup Dillon had been sitting. With Brett Pesce and Johnathan Kovacevic unavailable on Thursday, the Devils needed him to do more than just take a regular shift. He helped create the tying goal, and Kolyachonok said the two talked before the game to make sure they were on the same page. “I thought in lots of ways, Dilly had his best game of the season here tonight,” Keefe said. “He’s just competing hard, and he’s a very proud guy.” Dillon finished the game with an assist, a plus-two rating, two shots, two blocks, and four hits in 18:31. Keefe praised Dillon’s “character, leadership, presence, perspective,” and talked about the relationships he has with everyone from the younger players to the guys who’ve been here for years. “He’s central in it all,” Keefe said. item.title: Assessing Evan Phillips’ Singing With The Atlanta Braves
item.description: The Atlanta Braves signed Evan Phillips to a three-year, $35 million contract , bolstering one of the best bullpens in MLB. Phillips will become a high-leverage arm for the Braves in the back end of the bullpen. While he’s a huge addition on his own, the Phillips signing raises other questions Atlanta needs to answer. Phillips has battled injuries and has only thrown 31.2 innings across 38 appearances over the past two seasons . However, when he has pitched, Phillips has been effective. Since 2025, he has a 2.84 ERA (151 ERA+) and 39 strikeouts to just eight total walks. If he can stay healthy, Phillips will become a major addition to the bullpen. His addition provides a clearer vision for other offseason moves, particularly with pitching. Welcome back to #BravesCountry , @EvanPhillips36 ! pic.twitter.com/NEbhgVBdYy — Atlanta Braves (@Braves) November 12, 2026 The Phillips Signing May Be Atlanta’s Way of Moving On From Iglesias Iglesias has been the Braves’ closer over the past two seasons. Iglesias is a free agent, and the Phillips signing may signal Atlanta is moving on. Last offseason, the Braves inked a three-year deal with Robert Suarez, who closed for the San Diego Padres. Suarez didn’t close during his first season in Atlanta, but he could step back into that role. The Braves closer finished fifth in NL Reliever of the Year voting, including two third-place votes. Iglesias was an NL All-Star this season, posting a 2.55 ERA and 34 saves in 37 opportunities. At 36, Iglesias is getting older, but he’s still effective. Phillips’ signing doesn’t rule out the possibility of Iglesias returning, as the Braves may have other plans for one of their current bullpen arms. The NL Reliever of the Year ballot pic.twitter.com/NzLyhMLTTF — Bob Nightengale (@BNightengale) November 12, 2026 Fuentes Is Heading Back to the Rotation and Phillips Fills His Bullpen Spot Didier Fuentes rose through Atlanta’s minor league system as a starting pitcher. When he debuted in 2025, that was the role he played. All four of his big-league appearances last season were starts. This season, things changed as Fuentes spent most of the season out of the bullpen. It was a success, as Fuentes posted a 2.45 ERA and 92 strikeouts in 73.1 innings pitched. While he was great out of the bullpen, the Braves want him to be a starter once again. The plan is for him to join the rotation in 2027. Regardless of what transpires, Atlanta has ensured that they have one of the top bullpens in MLB next season and beyond. There are other holes on the roster, but the bullpen should be a strength for the Braves in 2027. By signing Evan Phillips, the Braves have filled one their bullpen voids with another high-leverage option. Didier Fuentes' role will be determined after the Braves stretch him out as a starter during Spring Training. Raisel Iglesias remains a free agent. — Mark Bowman (@mlbbowman) November 12, 2026 Atlanta gets the offseason started with a key bullpen addition. What they do between

item.title: Timberwolves’ Practices Lift LaMelo Ball to New Playmaking Heights
item.description: Minnesota Timberwolves guard LaMelo Ball (1) celebrates against the Dallas Mavericks in the second half at Target Center. | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Daniel Benjamin, Editor All it took was two Minnesota Timberwolves practices to make LaMelo Ball look like the floor general the team hoped they were getting when they traded for Ball this summer . The timing of the practices was key — rare back-to-back sessions the team was able to conduct because they had three days off in the middle of a Timberwolves’ record eight-game homestand . For the first time since Anthony Edwards ‘ surgery, the team had a chance to step back, take a breath, and work on how they want to play in Edwards’ absence . Assistant coach Paolo Prigioni told the media that the Wolves “really took advantage of these two days” of practice, and it showed, particularly in Ball’s play Thursday. He finished with 22 points and a season-high nine assists as the Wolves throttled a good Dallas team 133-94. LaMelo Ball Controlled the Game From the Opening Tip On the Mavericks’ first possession, 15 seconds after the opening tip, Ball found Jonathan Kuminga for a layup on a textbook pick-and-roll. Whether that was a set play from the Timberwolves’ practices or not, it seemed to get Ball going. In the next two minutes, Ball found Kuminga and Jaden McDaniels for dunks, then hit a three-pointer. He finished with six threes on the night, but this game was more about his playmaking than his shotmaking. Ball has had big scoring nights in his 12 games with Minnesota, including a 34-point performance in a Nov. 2 win over Milwaukee. But he had never had more than eight assists before Thursday. Against Dallas, he had eight in the first half and finished with nine despite sitting most of the second half and playing just 25 minutes total. Ball didn’t need those two Timberwolves’ practices to improve as a scorer — he gets plenty of shots up on his own time. He needed the Timberwolves’ practices to improve his chemistry and connection with his teammates, and step up as a playmaker in the wake of Edwards’ injury . The Ball-Gobert Connection Showed Signs of Life Minnesota Timberwolves center Rudy Gobert (27) and guard LaMelo Ball (1) enjoy a moment after a break from action with the Milwaukee Bucks in the fourth quarter at Target Center. Photo Credit: Bruce Kluckhohn, Imagn Images via Reuters Connect Ball also showed an improved connection with Rudy Gobert on Thursday, a development that’s incredibly important to the Timberwolves moving forward. One of the team’s aspirations in acquiring Ball was to unlock the 7-foot-1 Gobert as a lob threat like he was in Utah. The early returns on that have not been great. The timing between Ball and Gobert has looked off, and the combination of Ball’s penchant for quick, no-look passes and Gobert’s iffy hands has led to many balls sailing out of bounds. There was one of those Thursday, as Ball fired a pass that went right between Gobert’s big mitts early in the game. Bu
item.content:encoded: Minnesota Timberwolves guard LaMelo Ball (1) celebrates against the Dallas Mavericks in the second half at Target Center. | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Daniel Benjamin, Editor All it took was two Minnesota Timberwolves practices to make LaMelo Ball look like the floor general the team hoped they were getting when they traded for Ball this summer . He needed the Timberwolves’ practices to improve his chemistry and connection with his teammates, and step up as a playmaker in the wake of Edwards’ injury . The Ball-Gobert Connection Showed Signs of Life Minnesota Timberwolves center Rudy Gobert (27) and guard LaMelo Ball (1) enjoy a moment after a break from action with the Milwaukee Bucks in the fourth quarter at Target Center. Photo Credit: Bruce Kluckhohn, Imagn Images via Reuters Connect Ball also showed an improved connection with Rudy Gobert on Thursday, a development that’s incredibly important to the Timberwolves moving forward. One of the team’s aspirations in acquiring Ball was to unlock the 7-foot-1 Gobert as a lob threat like he was in Utah. The early returns on that have not been great. The timing between Ball and Gobert has looked off, and the combination of Ball’s penchant for quick, no-look passes and Gobert’s iffy hands has led to many balls sailing out of bounds. There was one of those Thursday, as Ball fired a pass that went right between Gobert’s big mitts early in the game. But after that, Ball and Gobert connected on two lobs — one that Gobert dunked emphatically with two hands and another that he laid in softly. Improving those lobs was likely a focus in the Timberwolves’ practices because, with Edwards out, they need more scoring from Gobert. He finished with just nine points on Thursday, but, like Ball, he played limited minutes in the blowout win. On a per-minute basis, his production was encouraging. The Last Word The way Ball got everyone going against Dallas was contagious, and six Timberwolves scored in double figures. They had 33 assists on 52 made baskets as a team and shot 58% from the field. By almost every metric, it was their top offensive performance of the season. Videos of practices have shown the Timberwolves’ chemistry , including a recent one in which Edwards cut up with his teammates despite being on crutches . Having a couple of days to get together and work on things seems to have only made this 9-3 team better and solidified Ball’s place as the team’s offensive leader with Ant out. item.title: 'It was actually a self-own': ESPN reporter has unique theory on 24-team CFP
item.description: Credit: The Play-By-Play LIVE As more information comes out about the expansion of the College Football Playoff to 24 teams, one thing is certain: Almost nobody wanted this. Just this week, The Athletic reported that even ESPN, which has broadcast rights to the entire tournament, didn’t support the idea . And a Nielsen survey showed that 90 percent of respondents who considered themselves college football fans also didn’t support it—which CFP executive director Rich Clark acknowledged ( and ignored) this week. Yet here we are, with the first 24-team bracket set to arrive next winter . And ESPN’s Dan Wetzel believes that by chasing “credibility” with the weekly rankings show, the committee dug a grave for its own credibility and forced itself to expand to please critics. “One of the reasons we expanded this Playoff is by doing these weekly rankings over the years. They absolutely killed the credibility of the committee,” Wetzel said Wednesday on The College GameDay Podcast . “And so every week, these things come out, it’s literally a half-baked pie, and then you let everybody tee off on you. And so it is either, in the media, people who are going to get far more engagement on the outrage algorithm of saying, ‘This is the dumbest committee of all time,’ they did this, or they did that. Or, these coaches who sit around and complain about, ‘We’re just not getting respect because we’re not this or we’re not that.'” By opening up its deliberations to scrutiny, the committee ultimately may have revealed its own shortcomings. Beyond the complaints that Wetzel highlights, even genuine analysis of the rankings each week would underscore faulty arguments. The week-to-week selection of teams that qualify for the postseason is far less exact than a big, fancy rankings show makes it out to be. And Wetzel believes that the committee was so sensitive to the criticism it faced that it inevitably embraced arguments from teams and conferences that used these inexact rankings cases to argue that, in fact, more teams were worthy of a Playoff berth. “ There’s an entire economy on ripping the hell out of the committee , which undermines the value of the committee and undermines that this Playoff isn’t successful, and hence we need to expand the Playoff,” Wetzel explained. “It was not an organized activity. It was actually a self-own by the Playoff people who wanted this to work. But you can draw a pretty quick line between deciding we’re going to put out a half-baked ranking and why we went from a four-team Playoff to a 24-team Playoff in four short years. And part of it is they just allowed this to be smashed up, and it’s like, who the hell cares where they’re ranked right now? We’ll find out.” The committee doesn’t seem to agree. The rankings will continue even under the 24-team format, though host Rece Davis acknowledged they need to be “ reimagined ” so as not to bore the audience with a long list of mediocre teams in the lower seeds. But in its quest to spark conv

item.title: More Americans are playing golf than ever before. Here's why
item.description: Golf has officially reached a new high-water mark. And this time, Tiger Woods isn't the only reason. More Americans are playing golf than at any point in history. But the game's latest surge isn't just happening on the golf course. It's happening in garages, sports bars, indoor simulators and entertainment venues across the country. An estimated 30.8 million Americans played golf on a traditional golf course in 2026, according to research from the National Golf Foundation (NGF). That's an increase of 1.7 million players over the previous year and enough to surpass the sport's previous record of 30.6 million, established in 2003 during the height of the Tiger phenomenon. Only this time, it has done so under a very different set of circumstances. The 1.7 million net increase represents the second-largest one-year gain in golf participation on record. Since 2019, before the pandemic fundamentally changed how Americans spent their leisure time, the number of on-course golfers has climbed by 6.5 million, a remarkable 27 percent increase. Golf isn't simply recovering. It's expanding. And the most interesting part of the story may be where people are playing. The golf landscape of 2026 looks considerably different from the one that existed in 2003. Back then, the United States had more than 2,000 additional golf courses compared with today. item.content:encoded: Golf has officially reached a new high-water mark. And this time, Tiger Woods isn't the only reason. More Americans are playing golf than at any point in history. But the game's latest surge isn't just happening on the golf course. It's happening in garages, sports bars, indoor simulators and entertainment venues across the country. An estimated 30.8 million Americans played golf on a traditional golf course in 2026, according to research from the National Golf Foundation (NGF). That's an increase of 1.7 million players over the previous year and enough to surpass the sport's previous record of 30.6 million, established in 2003 during the height of the Tiger phenomenon. Think about that for a moment. More than two decades after Woods helped transform golf into a mainstream sporting obsession, the game has reached another milestone. Only this time, it has done so under a very different set of circumstances. The 1.7 million net increase represents the second-largest one-year gain in golf participation on record. Since 2019, before the pandemic fundamentally changed how Americans spent their leisure time, the number of on-course golfers has climbed by 6.5 million, a remarkable 27 percent increase. Golf isn't simply recovering. It's expanding. And the most interesting part of the story may be where people are playing. The golf landscape of 2026 looks considerably different from the one that existed in 2003. Back then, the United States had more than 2,000 additional golf courses compared with today. The economy was strong, Tiger was dominating the sport, and social media hadn't yet become the all-consuming competitor for people's attention that it is now. Golf had more places to play, but fewer ways to experience the game. Today, the sport is setting participation records despite having fewer traditional golf facilities and competing with an extraordinary range of entertainment options. The game has also become more accessible in ways that would have been difficult to imagine during the original Tiger boom. You no longer need to reserve a tee time, find three playing partners or commit five hours to enjoy golf. You can grab a bucket of balls at a driving range, rent a simulator bay with friends, visit a golf entertainment venue or work on your swing in your own garage. Golf has expanded beyond the fairways, and the numbers tell the story. While traditional golf participation reached an all-time high, off-course golf established a record of its own. An estimated 39.6 million Americans engaged with golf away from traditional courses in 2026, visiting driving ranges, indoor simulator facilities and golf entertainment venues. This category has established a new participation record every year since the NGF began tracking it in 2014. Growth has moderated from the early years, largely because fewer large-scale golf entertainment venues have opened recently. But one segment continues to spread: golf simulators. They're appearing in commercial entertainment facilities, country clubs, public golf courses, private homes and even garages. For some, they're a convenient way to practice. For others, they're an alternative to the traditional golf experience. And for an increasing number of people, they're simply a fun way to spend an evening with friends. That audience barely existed during the 2003 participation peak. At the time, off-course golf largely meant hitting balls at a driving range. The NGF estimates that only 5 million to 6 million Americans participated exclusively in range-based golf. Today, the off-course universe is nearly eight times larger. The definition of a golfer has also changed, and so has the business of golf. Perhaps the most revealing development is the growing number of people who participate in both versions of the game. They're known as the "Dualies." These are golfers who enjoy traditional green-grass golf but also participate in off-course golf activities. More than two-thirds of all on-course golfers now fall into this category. Their numbers have increased 42 percent since 2019 and 11 percent since 2024. That's an important distinction because Dualies aren't simply casual visitors who occasionally pick up a club. They're among the most engaged participants in the sport. Compared with other golfers, they play more frequently and spend more money on the game. In other words, they're helping fuel both sides of the golf economy. The traditional golf course remains the centerpiece of the sport, but the simulator, driving range and entertainment venue are increasingly becoming part of the same golf-centric lifestyle. And that's a significant shift for an industry that historically defined participation almost exclusively by rounds played on a golf course. Add traditional and off-course participation together, and the numbers become even more impressive. A combined 49.5 million Americans participated in golf in 2026, another all-time high. That's nearly 50 million people engaging with the game in one form or another. It's also a much broader audience than the one that existed during the Tiger Woods boom. Some are dedicated players chasing lower handicaps. Others are occasional golfers who enjoy a weekend round. Some may never set foot on a traditional golf course, preferring the convenience and social atmosphere of a simulator or entertainment venue. But they're all part of the same expanding golf ecosystem. For golf operators, equipment manufacturers, instructors, retailers and developers, that creates opportunities well beyond the traditional tee sheet. It also suggests that the future of the game may depend as much on attracting new participants to alternative golf experiences as it does on getting more people onto traditional courses. The challenge will be converting that enthusiasm into long-term participation while keeping the game accessible, affordable and enjoyable. There was a time when golf's growth seemed tied almost entirely to one extraordinary player. Tiger Woods inspired a generation, brought new attention to the sport and helped propel participation to record levels in 2003. Today, the game has reached an even higher peak without the same singular catalyst. Instead, golf is benefiting from a combination of factors: increased interest in outdoor recreation, pandemic-era participation gains that have endured, technology, entertainment-driven venues and a broader definition of what it means to play the game. The traditional round of golf isn't going anywhere. If anything, the record 30.8 million on-course participants demonstrate that its appeal remains remarkably strong. But golf is no longer confined to 18 holes, a scorecard and a tee time. It's a driving range after work, a simulator on a rainy afternoon, a night out with friends or a weekend round with family. The game has found more ways to fit into people's lives, and millions of Americans have responded. Nearly 50 million participants later, golf has reached a new high-water mark. The remarkable thing isn't just that the sport has broken its record. It's that there are now more ways than ever to be part of it. Golf is booming again. And this time, the entire golf universe is along for the ride. Adam Schupak is a senior writer for Golfweek, covering the PGA Tour. item.title: Reading missing key players for Stockport game
item.description: Reading have played away from home for five matches across all competitions [Shutterstock] Reading head coach Leam Richardson has said he will be without a number of key players for their game against Stockport County on Saturday. The Royals will miss some players because of injury, suspension and international call-ups as they travel away to take on the second-placed Hatters. Richardson's team sit sixth in League One with six wins from 14 games. They beat Peterborough United 5-0 in the FA Cup on Saturday before losing on penalties to Bristol Rovers on Tuesday in the Jersey Mike's Trophy. "[Jacob] Brown is still struggling with his ribs coming off the back of Wednesday [against Oxford]," Richardson told BBC Radio Berkshire. "Jeriel [Dorsett] has been called up to Montserrat but he's had a little knock as well so we'll be without the pair of them at the weekend. "Paudie [O'Connor] is at five [yellow cards] so that'll be him suspended as well - it's a huge [miss] as he's been really consistent and reliable for us. "He's a big personality on the pitch and off the pitch so it's disappointing because I didn't think it was a booking as well on Wednesday night in the Oxford game, but is what it is. "We've got to make sure we overcome, adapt and make sure we prepare as well as possible for these games." Reading will also be without injured defender Josh Knight and midfielder Andy Rinomhota, who Richardson believes will serve his suspension for picking up five yellow cards while on international duty with Zimbabwe. Reading's match at Stockport on Saturday will be their fifth consecutive away game across all competitions, last playing at Select Car Leasing Stadium in late October. Richardson said the club have had to carefully plan their travel and recovery in recent weeks as they played at Plymouth, Oxford, Peterborough, Bristol and now in Greater Manchester this weekend. "We've had to make sure we're diligent with our travelling and everything else with our preparation," he added. "I'm really looking forward to it and think it'd be a really good game. Fingers crossed we're prepared and get a positive result to finish these away days in this block off. "They've been in the play-offs and have been recruiting very well, spending money on different players and always challenged at the top end of this level which is what every club is after. "They're a really good team as well and are well-coached so it'll be a really good game." All the latest Reading news

item.title: No. 10 BYU vs. Baylor: How to watch, listen to or stream Saturday’s matchup
item.description: BYU Cougars players warm up before a football game against the Notre Dame Fighting Irish at LaVell Edwards Stadium in Provo on Saturday, Oct. 17, 2026. | Tess Crowley, Deseret News No. 10 BYU (7-2, 4-2) vs. Baylor (6-3, 4-2) Kickoff: Saturday, 1:30 p.m. MST Venue: LaVell Edwards Stadium (capacity: 62,073) TV: Fox Livestream : foxsports.com/live Radio: KSL 1160 AM/102.7 FM/BYU Radio Sirius XM 166 Series: BYU leads, 3-2 The trends For BYU: The Cougars are coming off a painful rivalry loss at Utah, but their College Football Playoff hopes remain alive after only dropping one spot to No. 10 in the latest CFP poll. If BYU wants any shot at playoff action, however, it needs to take care of business down the stretch, starting Saturday against an upstart, inspired Baylor squad. How the Cougars handle the Bears after last week’s letdown will reveal a great deal about their CFP hopes. BYU is scoring 31.0 points per game and allowing 19.8 points per contest, but has not won the turnover battle in more than a month. For Baylor: All appeared lost for the Bears upon firing head coach Dave Aranda in October, but interim Joe Klanderman has managed to rally Baylor for two convincing wins since then to remain in the thick of the Big 12 title chase. Baylor is scoring 31.9 points per game and allowing 17.0 points per game. Quotable BYU Cougars head coach Kalani Sitake walks onto the field for pre-game warmups before a game against Arizona State at LaVell Edwards Stadium in Provo on Saturday, October 31, 2026. | Lukas Katilius, Deseret News “We can’t let the Utah loss linger into (this) week, but what we can do is use it as motivation to get better. We appreciate all the fans and everyone who supports us. We know we can play better, and it is my job to get these guys playing at a higher level.” — BYU coach Kalani Sitake “Our margin for error is razor-thin. You can’t afford mental busts or lapses in effort against a top-10 team.” — Baylor coach Joe Klanderman Next up BYU: at Kansas on Nov. 21 Baylor: vs. Texas Tech on Nov. 21 BYU schedule Sept. 5 — defeated Utah Tech, 63-7 Sept. 12 — defeated Arizona, 28-17 Sept. 19 — defeated Colorado State, 41-23 Oct. 3 — defeated TCU, 17-10 Oct. 9 — defeated Iowa State, 24-10 Oct. 17 — defeated Notre Dame, 28-24 Oct. 24 — lost at UCF, 39-31 Oct. 31 — defeated Arizona State, 27-20 Nov. 7 — lost at Utah, 28-20 Nov. 14 — Baylor, 1:30 p.m. MST Nov. 21 — at Kansas Nov. 28 — Cincinnati

item.title: Wyndham Clark admits what he really thinks of Jackson Koivun after watching him play at the Presidents Cup
item.description: Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images Wyndham Clark got to witness what Jackson Koivun is really like as a golfer and a person at the Presidents Cup back in September at Medinah. The United States won the Presidents Cup in the end, but the 17-13 scoreline was a lot closer than many predicted prior to the event. Clark struggled for his best form throughout the week at Medinah, but Koivun was one of the stars for Team USA. Jackson Koivun went unbeaten throughout the week at the Presidents Cup , winning two and halving one of his three matches. Wyndham Clark got a first-hand view that week of how the 21-year-old goes about his business both on and off the golf course. And now the two-time US Open winner has opened up on his true feelings about the talented young American. What Wyndham Clark thinks of Jackson Koivun after watching him at the Presidents Cup Koivun is keen to play on the US Ryder Cup team in 2027, and his performance at the Presidents Cup surely means that he is almost guaranteed to be at Adare Manor next year. The 21-year-old obviously has the talent and mentality required to succeed at the very highest level of the game, but what does someone who has already reached that level think about the youngster’s chances of doing exactly that? During an appearance on the Dan on Golf YouTube channel, Clark was asked about Koivun as a player and a person and whether he acts older than his tender years. “ No, he’s a kid, “ Clark insisted. “ I tell you what, I have nothing but praise for that kid. He’s so talented. Obviously, he showed it off at the Presidents Cup. “ You know, a lot of people asked a lot of us what we thought of his pick and I said it somewhere, I was like, ‘He’s our secret weapon’. Because I think, you know, he’s a young kid that has nothing to lose. No pressure, really. “ And then, going up against him as, you know, a seasoned veteran, someone like Si Woo Kim. There is more pressure on Si Woo. “ You don’t want to lose to the kid, right? And sure enough, that’s what happens. So, yeah, nothing but respect for him. “ He is a kid, but I love the kid. He’s awesome. He’s gonna have a lot of success out here. “ That is a seriously glowing reference of Jackson Koivun, and he will surely be very proud indeed when he hears those remarks from Wyndham Clark. It will be fascinating to watch how Koivun performs on the PGA Tour in 2027 with his attempts to make the Ryder Cup team at Adare Manor making for a seriously interesting subplot.

item.title: Red Wings Must End the John Gibson Experiment in Net
item.description: The Detroit Red Wings once led 4-1 against the Florida Panthers on Thursday night. It ended in a 5-4 loss for Detroit. With the loss, the Red Wings have now lost five straight games, but the streak may not be the biggest story. John Gibson is. Gibson stopped 24 of the 29 shots he faced in Florida, and he gave up five goals. That was not a one-night problem. Detroit has played 20 games this season and Gibson has appeared in 13 of them, and he carries a 4-7-1 record with a 3.58 goals-against average and a .862 save percentage , along with zero shutouts. With another bad outing on the pile, it might be time for the Red Wings to finally do something about it. Nov 10, 2026; St. Louis, Missouri, USA; Detroit Red Wings goaltender John Gibson (36) defends the net against the St. Louis Blues during the second period at Enterprise Center. Mandatory Credit: Jeff Curry-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Detroit Red Wings need to end the John Gibson experiment now The Red Wings are in last place in the Atlantic Division with a 7-10-3 record and 17 points . Detroit has a better chance to win in net right now with Daniil Tarasov, Michal Postava, or Trey Augustine. There is no doubt that Gibson has been a major reason why the Red Wings have been losing. Look, the forward group is not deep by any means. With that being said, Gibson has not played well at all for Detroit this season. Who cares if he has a $6.4 million contract for the remainder of the season. The Red Wings need to seriously consider just scratching him until they can find a trade partner for him, or better yet place him on waivers. Calling up Trey Augustine or Michal Postava would be more beneficial to the team anyways Calling up Trey Augustine or Michal Postava from the Grand Rapids Griffins would be more beneficial to the growth of this hockey team than head coach Todd McLellan continuing to put Gibson between the pipes night in and night out. The Red Wings face the Tampa Bay Lightning on the road on Saturday. If they play Gibson again, this franchise is unserious about its goalie situation and cares more about tanking for a draft pick.

item.title: Four games that matter for Oregon's Big Ten title chances in Week 11
item.description: Having suffered three losses before the calendar flipped to November, the Oregon Ducks find themselves scrapping and clawing to make the Big Ten championship game, hoping to give themselves a shot at the College Football Playoff. It's not an enviable spot to be in, as the Ducks need to receive some help in order to reach the conference title game — but it's the spot that Oregon has put itself in. They've done their part in digging themselves out of a hole, winning two straight must-wins against Northwestern and Ohio State. The wins must continue in the final three regular-season games, home contests against Michigan and Washington and road date with Michigan State. If they don't go 3-0, nothing else matters and the Ducks will be packing their bags for a no-name bowl game in roughly a month. If they don't get some help, and the CFP Committee doesn't deem them worthy of receiving an at-large bid to the 12-team field, that same result will occur. Help is very much needed, and Week 11 is the most important week of them all. Last week, there were ten teams with two or fewer losses in Big Ten play. Now, after Minnesota and Northwestern loss, that number is down to eight. Oregon is joined by five other teams with exactly two conference losses and hoping to be joined by a sixth after Week 11. Tiebreakers will almost certainly come into the picture. Before we get too far ahead of ourselves, let's break down the four games that matter towards Oregon's chances of making the Big Ten title game in Week 11, assuming the Ducks take care of business against the Wolverines . Illinois Fighting Illini vs. No. 4 UCLA Bruins (Friday) When: 6:00 p.m. PT | | Friday Where: Rose Bowl | | Pasadena, CA TV: Fox Why it matters: This one's simple: UCLA wins and Illinois is essentially eliminated from the Big Ten title race with their third loss. The reason this matters for the Ducks is that the Fighting Illini hold the head-to-head tiebreaker after beating the Ducks in Champaign in October, Oregon's third loss of the year and second in conference. If Illinois miraculously wins on Friday night at the Rose Bowl over the undefeated Bruins, Duck fans should worry just a bit, but not too much. The Fighting Illini still have to play Iowa and Northwestern to finish the year. As long as they don't go undefeated, the Ducks will be fine. UCLA is basically a shoo-in as a representative in the Big Ten title game, so them winning on Friday doesn't mean anything for Oregon. Wisconsin Badgers @ Maryland Terrapins When: 9:00 a.m. PT Where: SECU Stadium | | College Park, MD TV: FS1 Why it matters: Wisconsin is another squad with two conference losses, and the tiebreaker scenario could get quite complicated. Assuming Oregon wins out, the Ducks and Badgers have the same 2-1 record against common conference opponents. From there, it'd go to the record against the highest-finishing conference opponent, but both teams would've beaten the same common opponents (USC and Michigan State) and lost to t
