Illinois Fighting Illini vs. No. 4 UCLA Bruins (Friday) When: 6:00 p.m. PT | | Friday Where: Rose Bowl | | Pasadena, CA TV: Fox Why it matters: This one's simple: UCLA wins and Illinois is essentially eliminated from the Big Ten title race with their third loss. The reason this matters for the Ducks is that the Fighting Illini hold the head-to-head tiebreaker after beating the Ducks in Champaign in October, Oregon's third loss of the year and second in conference. If Illinois miraculously wins on Friday night at the Rose Bowl over the undefeated Bruins, Duck fans should worry just a bit, but not too much. The Fighting Illini still have to play Iowa and Northwestern to finish the year. As long as they don't go undefeated, the Ducks will be fine. UCLA is basically a shoo-in as a representative in the Big Ten title game, so them winning on Friday doesn't mean anything for Oregon. Wisconsin Badgers @ Maryland Terrapins When: 9:00 a.m. PT Where: SECU Stadium | | College Park, MD TV: FS1 Why it matters: Wisconsin is another squad with two conference losses, and the tiebreaker scenario could get quite complicated. Assuming Oregon wins out, the Ducks and Badgers have the same 2-1 record against common conference opponents. From there, it'd go to the record against the highest-finishing conference opponent, but both teams would've beaten the same common opponents (USC and Michigan State) and lost to the same opponent (UCLA). Then, the tiebreaker would go to the cumulative conference winning percentage of all conference opponents, something that won't be certain until the end of the regular season. To eliminate all of that potential confusion, an upset from the Terrapins would help the Ducks out tremendously. No. 18 USC Trojans vs. No. 9 Indiana Hoosiers When: 12:30 p.m. PT Where: Memorial Stadium | | Bloomington, IN TV: CBS Why it matters: This is the biggest one, and it's unfortunate that it's at the same time as Oregon's bout with Michigan. Duck fans, it might be worth rocking the two TV set-up if you're able to, as it holds a ton of weight in terms of the Ducks' Big Ten title chances. The Hoosiers are currently 5-1 in conference. If they win out, they face UCLA in the conference championship. But a loss to USC would knock them down to the two-loss crew and give Oregon the tie-breaker, as the Ducks would have a better record against common opponents thanks to their win over the Trojans. Oregon winning on Saturday is big, but arch-rival USC winning in Bloomington would put the Ducks in the driver's seat for the Big Ten title game. Just this week, Duck fans will have to root hard for the Trojans. Purdue Boilermakers @ Iowa Hawkeyes When: 4:30 p.m. PT Where: Kinnick Stadium | | Iowa City, IA TV: NBC Why it matters: Iowa is in a similar spot as Wisconsin, holding two conference losses with a relatively light remaining schedule of Purdue, Illinois and Nebraska remaining. With the same record against common opponents, the tie-breaker with Oregon (assuming both the Ducks and Hawkeyes win out) would go to the record against the highest common opponent in the standings. That's likely to be Ohio State, a team that Oregon beat and Iowa lost to. But if the Buckeyes crumble down the stretch, that could change and put the Ducks in jeopardy of losing a tie-breaker to Iowa. This would be another miraculous upset, but Purdue getting a win at Kinnick Stadium would further clear the path for Oregon. Contact/Follow @Ducks_Wire on X (formerly Twitter) and like our page on Facebook to follow ongoing coverage of Oregon Ducks news, notes, and opinion s. item.title: ‘Lean Strongly Toward (Kyrie) Irving Staying Put’ – NBA Insider Deals a Blow To Heat, Rockets in Trade Sweepstakes for Mavericks Star
item.description: ‘Lean Strongly Toward (Kyrie) Irving Staying Put’ – NBA Insider Deals a Blow To Heat, Rockets in Trade Sweepstakes for Mavericks Star Amid speculation surrounding Kyrie Irving’s future, The Athletic’s Sam Amick believes that the 34-year-old will likely remain with the Dallas Mavericks through the Feb. 11 trade deadline. The NBA insider made that call Friday, one day after the Mavericks’ blowout loss in Minnesota, even while reporting that rival teams continue to rank Irving first among the players who could reshape the playoff race. Why Insider Sees Kyrie Irving Staying With the Dallas Mavericks Amick built his case around what is working in Dallas rather than around any one suitor. Miami has been reported as a team monitoring Irving, while Houston has also been floated as a possible fit if Dallas ever makes him available. Amick led his latest trade-watch column with Irving, roughly three months before the deadline, and he did not skip past the lopsided result from the night before. “Kyrie Irving may not be traded before the deadline, what with the Mavericks (7-5) looking better than expected and their 34-year-old point guard fitting in so well alongside their young franchise centerpiece, 19-year-old Cooper Flagg.” Amick pointed to the larger sample. By his count, the Mavericks are 7-3 this season when Irving plays and have lost both games he missed. But Amick wrote that the start in Dallas has not changed how rival teams see Irving. “Yet when you talk to rival teams about players who would truly change the playoff landscape if they were dealt, and who are widely expected to generate serious interest because of that belief, Irving still tops the list. Never mind that the Mavericks, and Irving for that matter, have shown no signs of wanting a split. Quite the opposite, in fact.” READ MORE: ‘It’s So Bad,’ ‘Have You Ever Seen That Drastic of a Drop-off?’ — NBA Champion Urges Knicks To ‘Move On’ From Mikal Bridges After Abysmal 2-Point Night Irving’s contract helps explain why the interest persists. He holds a $42.4 million player option for next season and can become a free agent this summer if he declines it. “The lack of a long-term deal between the Mavs and Irving, all by itself, justifies the outside interest,” Amick wrote. So does his form. Irving missed all of last season after tearing his left ACL in early March 2025, and Amick noted that “the fact that Irving still looks like Irving, after all he has been through, has only added to the intrigue.” Asked about the rumors Monday, Irving told reporters, “I let the team know out of my own mouth that these trade rumors, anything that’s going on with me, do not let this infiltrate our locker room. Don’t let this get in the way of what we have building here.” READ MORE: ‘Why Can’t We Have Nice Things?’ ‘I Just Talked Myself In’ — Bill Simmons Laments Stephen Curry’s Injury Setback Halting Warriors’ Momentum Amick also explained why Dallas wants to get the most out of Irving. But the odds of Irving being traded are likely notably less – if not nonexistent – if these Mavericks manage to play winning basketball,” he wrote. Even a quiet deadline would not settle Irving’s future in Dallas, because his player option leaves the next decision with him this summer. The Mavericks, meanwhile, sit 10th in the Western Conference at 7-5 after Thursday’s loss. This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network .

item.title: 'If conditions are flat, watch out': Mike Hesson finds a bizarre way to defend Babar Azam's struggles in Pakistan team
item.description: 'If conditions are flat, watch out': Mike Hesson finds a bizarre way to defend Babar Azam's struggles in Pakistan team originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: Mike Hesson says Pakistan batter Babar Azam's problems are being exaggerated and blames the conditions. Babar made 50 and 34 in the drawn first Test against Sri Lanka at Rawalpindi. He has now gone 42 innings without a Test century. Mike Hesson defends Babar Azam after Rawalpindi Test questions Pakistan head coach Mike Hesson has pushed back at the criticism of Babar Azam, arguing that his captain's scores say more about the pitch than about his batting. Hesson spoke after the first Test against Sri Lanka at Rawalpindi ended in a draw. He began by dismissing the value of Babar's first-innings fifty, then said the seam movement left any batter at risk. "Look, sometimes, those are condition-dependent. So I don't think the fifty he got in the first innings was a high-quality fifty. And you know, when the ball seams like that, sometimes it's going to have your number on it," Hesson said in a clip posted on X . Mike Hesson on Babar Azam form. 🗣️ "He averages over 50 in Test cricket this year, the highest by anyone who has played 10 innings. If the conditions are flat and he gets himself in, look out." — Sheri. (@CallMeSheri1_) November 13, 2026 Hesson then turned to the numbers and finished with a warning about what happens when Babar gets a flat pitch. "You look at Babar; he averages over 50 in Test cricket this year. It's the highest average for anybody who has played more than 10 innings. So to think he's got an issue is, I think, often overhyped. And I think, as I said, if the conditions are flat and he gets himself in, look out." MORE: India's 89 all-out at Bay Oval a 'trailer' for NZ Test series How did Babar Azam perform in the first Test vs Sri Lanka? Sri Lanka put Pakistan in to bat on a green surface on day one, and four batters reached fifty, two of them on debut. Tayyab Arif made 57 and Mohammad Taha 51, while Babar contributed the 50 his coach has now talked down. Saud Shakeel took it furthest with 93, and Pakistan declared 434 for 9. Sri Lanka answered with 446, with centuries from Dhananjaya de Silva and Kusal Mendis carrying them to a 12-run lead and leaving the match without a clear favorite. Pakistan began the final day 45 ahead and had to bat out the day rather than chase anything. The match ended in the draw everyone expected. Babar made 34 in that second innings, hitting six fours and adding 50 with Shakeel before Milan Rathnayaka set a leg-side trap and had him caught at short square leg. Kamindu Mendis had dropped him on 22. Salman Agha fell to the same plan for 13, and Pakistan finished the weather-hit match on 284 for 8. Hesson is right that the pitch had something in it, but Rathnayaka dismissed Babar with a planned leg-side trap rather than a seaming delivery with his name on it. item.title: The 2027 Lockout Preview – Overview
item.description: ST. PETERSBURG, FL - OCTOBER 26: Derek Jeter talks with Commissioner of Major League Baseball Robert D. Manfred prior to Game Three of the 2026 World Series presented by Capital One between the Milwaukee Brewers and the Tampa Bay Rays at Tropicana Field on Monday, October 26, 2026 in St. Petersburg, Florida. (Photo by Daniel Shirey/MLB Photos via Getty Images) | MLB Photos via Getty Images The 2026 season may not have been great for fans of the Toronto Blue Jays, but for baseball in general, it was a stellar year. While the books aren’t entirely opaque, direct revenue raised by the MLB is estimated at over $13B for the season, the highest ever, and continuing a steady trend line since the COVID shortened 2020 season of about 4-7% growth year over year. Three teams changed ownership this year – Tampa Bay, San Diego, and Los Angeles – selling for $1.7B, $3.9B, and $4B respectively, despite all three facing challenges ranging from the need for a new stadium, a small media market, and a complete overhaul after decades of irrelevance. And yet, despite all of this success, owners are expected to lock out the players on the final minute of December 1 st , 2026. Why would a business that is experiencing runaway success risk everything with the potential loss of games and revenue in 2027? How will the players respond? How certain are we that we’re going to see one side or the other fold and what is at sake for the future? This series will hopefully shed some light on what is often a confusing and opaque process before events start to unfold in real time. Or explain things you already know but give you a dedicated comment section to rail against the players/owners/system/TheMan. The Collective Bargaining Agreement This whole process revolves around the Collective Bargaining Agreement (CBA) between the MLB and the MLBPA. The CBA remains in force for five years and must be renegotiated after that time. The current CBA expires on Tuesday, December 1 st at 11:59PM which is why the expectation of when the lockout will begin is so precise. The CBA is a wide-ranging agreement which covers extremely consequential things like arbitration, free agency requirements, roster size as well as significantly less important elements like a mandatory chef in each clubhouse. Negotiations for the owners are headed by the MLB Deputy Commissioner Dan Halem and his team and the players are represented by MLBPA Executive Director Bruce Meyer and his team. Halem and MLB Commissioner Rob Manfred communicates with the 30 MLB owners and their specific representatives, and Meyer meets with the Executive Subcommittee and the 30 Team Player Representatives. The players in theory only need a straight majority out of the 38 votes from the Executive Subcommittee and the Team Player Representatives. item.content:encoded: ST. PETERSBURG, FL - OCTOBER 26: Derek Jeter talks with Commissioner of Major League Baseball Robert D. Manfred prior to Game Three of the 2026 World Series presented by Capital One between the Milwaukee Brewers and the Tampa Bay Rays at Tropicana Field on Monday, October 26, 2026 in St. Petersburg, Florida. (Photo by Daniel Shirey/MLB Photos via Getty Images) | MLB Photos via Getty Images The 2026 season may not have been great for fans of the Toronto Blue Jays, but for baseball in general, it was a stellar year. While the books aren’t entirely opaque, direct revenue raised by the MLB is estimated at over $13B for the season, the highest ever, and continuing a steady trend line since the COVID shortened 2020 season of about 4-7% growth year over year. Three teams changed ownership this year – Tampa Bay, San Diego, and Los Angeles – selling for $1.7B, $3.9B, and $4B respectively, despite all three facing challenges ranging from the need for a new stadium, a small media market, and a complete overhaul after decades of irrelevance. And yet, despite all of this success, owners are expected to lock out the players on the final minute of December 1 st , 2026. Why would a business that is experiencing runaway success risk everything with the potential loss of games and revenue in 2027? How will the players respond? How certain are we that we’re going to see one side or the other fold and what is at sake for the future? This series will hopefully shed some light on what is often a confusing and opaque process before events start to unfold in real time. Or explain things you already know but give you a dedicated comment section to rail against the players/owners/system/TheMan. The Collective Bargaining Agreement This whole process revolves around the Collective Bargaining Agreement (CBA) between the MLB and the MLBPA. The CBA remains in force for five years and must be renegotiated after that time. The current CBA expires on Tuesday, December 1 st at 11:59PM which is why the expectation of when the lockout will begin is so precise. The CBA is a wide-ranging agreement which covers extremely consequential things like arbitration, free agency requirements, roster size as well as significantly less important elements like a mandatory chef in each clubhouse. Negotiations for the owners are headed by the MLB Deputy Commissioner Dan Halem and his team and the players are represented by MLBPA Executive Director Bruce Meyer and his team. Halem and MLB Commissioner Rob Manfred communicates with the 30 MLB owners and their specific representatives, and Meyer meets with the Executive Subcommittee and the 30 Team Player Representatives. In order to reach a decision, the owners need a 75% majority of votes, so 23 out of 30 owners. The players in theory only need a straight majority out of the 38 votes from the Executive Subcommittee and the Team Player Representatives. For example, in the last CBA negotiations in 2022, the 8 man Executive Subcommittee voted unanimously to reject the owners offer but lost the full vote by the Representatives 26-12. Lockout Versus Strike The terms are often used interchangeably and are both forms of work stoppages but there is a significant difference between the two. Strikes are player led work stoppages during which the players withhold their services. The last MLBPA led strike took place in 1994, specifically to block the implementation of a salary cap, which cancelled the rest of the season and post season and lasted until April 2, 1995. Lockouts are initiated by the owners, which means all player related activities and communications are halted, including trades, signings, training and access to team facilities until the lockout is lifted. The reasoning behind a lockout is that having hard deadlines provides teams leverage in the negotiations, as players will be pressured by not having contracts, job security or access for training and rehab resources to accept a contract more favourable to the owners. What Do They Want? Both sides have been preparing for a potential lockout for the last several years. A series of proposals have gone back and forth between the MLB and the MLBPA, mostly for the sake of media coverage and positioning, as each group looks to bring the public on their side. While the details can shift rapidly, each has outlined a broad agenda of their priorities. MLB Owners Key elements include: Salary Cap and Floor: Tied as a baseline requirement to all league proposals, MLB has proposed a hard salary cap of roughly $258.2 million and a salary floor of $180.2 million, paired with a 50/50 revenue split between owners and players to be implemented in 2028. Shorter Regular Season and Expended Playoffs: Reducing the regular season from 162 to 154 games starting in 2029 to provide a standard weekly off-day and a dedicated Monday broadcast window. Extending the Division Series to best-of-seven and allowing higher-seeded teams to pick their opponents. Roster & Offseason Changes: Weekly roster-setting windows, a 14-pitcher limit, Rule 5 draft adjustments, a reduced draft of 12 rounds excluding high school players, an international draft and an offseason transaction calendar featuring a winter quiet/frozen period. Free Agency and Wages: Increasing the minimum salary to $1M and decreasing the service time requirements from 6 to 5 years before qualifying for free agency. The key for the owners is that they are willing to offer all kinds of incentives for the players; things that are good for them like a year less of team control, having a day off every week built into the calendar, making it more likely good teams have deeper playoff runs, and increasing their potential post season earnings. However, the two red lights for the players are the glaring blaring siren of a salary cap, and the reduction in the draft allowing them to further shrink their farm systems without losing competitive balance with other teams. MLBPA Key elements include: Tax on Low-Spending Teams: A “competitive-integrity tax” targeting low-spending clubs (mirroring the luxury tax for high spenders). Higher Thresholds & Salaries: Raising the base Competitive Balance Tax (CBT) threshold to $300 million (up from $244 million), near-doubling player minimum salaries, and increasing local television revenue sharing. Also Expanding active rosters from 26 to 28 players for the first 15 days of the season. Reduced Service Time: allowing players over thirty to reach FA after 5 years. The key for the players is challenging the disparity in team payrolls in a way that doesn’t limit player earning potentials that a cap would, while expanding financial opportunities for younger players and players who earn MLB spots later in their careers. While the players proposal is more of a wish list, it is wrapped around one absolutely unshakable point, which is that the MLBPA will not consider a salary cap under any circumstances. While the Commissioner and his office have been trying to sell the cap and floor to the players by pointing out the proposed cap and floor would cost 8 teams about $580M in payroll, but it would compel 12 teams to raise their payrolls a little over $615M. While things will develop very quickly, the starting positions by both sides couldn’t be further apart. It also isn’t helped by the complete lack of trust in the MLB owners by the MLBPA. They have resisted every effort for any kind of consistent transparency in their revenue or financial situations, so the MLBPA rejects the owners position that small market teams are uncompetitive and there’s no other mechanism but a cap to re-establish parity. As Paul Beeston famously said: “Anyone who quotes profits of a baseball club is missing the point. Under generally accepted accounting principles, I can turn a $4 million profit into a $2 million loss, and I can get every national accounting firm to agree with me.” Even if the cap is tied directly to a 50/50 revenue split, there is absolutely no

item.title: In Disappointing and Injury-Riddled Season, Shohei Ohtani Finishes Second to Pete Crow-Armstrong in MVP Race
item.description: Oct 15, 2026; Los Angeles, California, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers designated hitter Shohei Ohtani (17) reacts after striking out during the fifth inning against the Milwaukee Brewers in game four of the NLCS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at Un… | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Augustus Oswald, Site Editor Los Ángeles Dodgers’ four-time Most Valuable Player Shohei Ohtani did not win a fifth award. Chicago Cubs center fielder Pete Crow Armstrong did , and deservedly so. Ohtani, who has two trophies from each league, finished in second place. It is the first time in four years that the baseball unicorn has not won the award, but it wasn’t for lack of effort. However, injuries played a huge part in his downfall. As a result, Armstrong filled the void and did an outstanding job, completing a 40/40 season. Shohei Ohtani is One of One The only player to have won more MVPs than Shohei Ohtani is Barry Bonds , who owns seven. For a while, it looked like Ohtani was making another run at history. At the end of June, Ohtani had close to 30 home runs and was hitting close to a .300 average. He was the threat that every pitcher dreads at the top of the lineup. But that wasn’t all; he maintained a 2.00 Earned Run Average as a starter in the Los Angeles rotation and was near the top of the league in inducing strikeouts. There hasn’t been a two-way player with that resume since Babe Ruth. item.content:encoded: Oct 15, 2026; Los Angeles, California, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers designated hitter Shohei Ohtani (17) reacts after striking out during the fifth inning against the Milwaukee Brewers in game four of the NLCS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at Un… | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Augustus Oswald, Site Editor Los Ángeles Dodgers’ four-time Most Valuable Player Shohei Ohtani did not win a fifth award. Chicago Cubs center fielder Pete Crow Armstrong did , and deservedly so. Ohtani, who has two trophies from each league, finished in second place. It is the first time in four years that the baseball unicorn has not won the award, but it wasn’t for lack of effort. However, injuries played a huge part in his downfall. As a result, Armstrong filled the void and did an outstanding job, completing a 40/40 season. Shohei Ohtani is One of One The only player to have won more MVPs than Shohei Ohtani is Barry Bonds , who owns seven. For a while, it looked like Ohtani was making another run at history. At the end of June, Ohtani had close to 30 home runs and was hitting close to a .300 average. He was the threat that every pitcher dreads at the top of the lineup. But that wasn’t all; he maintained a 2.00 Earned Run Average as a starter in the Los Angeles rotation and was near the top of the league in inducing strikeouts. There hasn’t been a two-way player with that resume since Babe Ruth. Sep 1, 2026; Los Angeles, California, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers designated hitter Shohei Ohtani (17) bats as St. Louis Cardinals catcher Leo Bernal (13) and home plate home plate umpire Alex MacKay (9) watch at Dodger Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Nightmare Finish It all fell apart at the beginning of July, when Ohtani was forced to opt out of the All-Star Game due to a sore knee. The injury persisted, and the consequences were most visible at the plate. After July 1, Ohtani barely stayed above a .200 batting average, driving in fewer than 20 runs, and only hit two home runs the rest of the season. It was obvious that he couldn’t drive off his back leg. Oct 15, 2026; Los Angeles, California, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers pitcher Shohei Ohtani (17) reacts after striking out during the first inning against the Milwaukee Brewers in game four of the NLCS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at Uniqlo Field at Dodger Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images TPX IMAGES OF THE DAY Moreover, Ohtani was swinging at fastballs he usually drives over 400 feet, and nearly every swing drew a shake of the arm or a wince of pain. In short, Ohtani was a shell of himself, even after a stint on the 15-day Injured List. Thus, winning awards. or, for that matter, a World Series was out of the question. The Last Word The loss of a chance at a fifth MVP should be a cautionary tale for both Ohtani and the Dodgers. The lack of communication regarding the condition of the superstar’s health is troubling. The insistence on throwing bullpen sessions after the knee issue popped up is downright baffling, particularly because both parties admitted that it was the act of throwing on the mound that caused the injury in the first place. It not only cost Ohtani the MVP but may have cost the Dodgers a chance at a three-peat as well. Going forward, discretion should be the better part of valor, even if the upcoming season appears to be abbreviated. Ohtani has already etched his name among the greatest players ever to grace the baseball diamond. But going forward, the Dodgers have to make a better effort to preserve the health of their superstar so that he can keep pursuing not only prestigious individual awards but more World Series rings. They have already seen the consequences i f they don’t put limitations on their Superman; he serves as his own Kryptonite. It doesn’t help his team either. President of Baseball Operations Andrew Friedman has said that “surgery is not on the table” for Baseball’s unicorn. That’s good news. However, the Dodgers are left to wonder what could have been, had Ohtani been more open about his physical well-being. Andrew Friedman said surgery is “not on the table” for Shohei Ohtani. Said it was “whack a mole” between the knee, then the biceps throughout the year. Friedman: “I fully expect him to pitch next year.” — Fabian Ardaya (@FabianArdaya) October 21, 2026 Crow-Armstrong deserves the MVP Award. He had an outstanding year, and his 40/40 season put the rest of the league on notice of what one can do when healthy. The earlier Ohtani learns that, the better it is for him…and the Dodgers. item.description: Foxborough, MA - October 18: New England Patriots wide receiver A.J. Brown warms up before the game. The New England Patriots played the New York Jets at Gillette Stadium on October 18, 2026. (Photo by Danielle Parhizkaran/The Boston Globe via Getty Images) | Boston Globe via Getty Images The light will be left on for running back Rhamondre Stevenson and wide receiver A.J. Brown. Both starters stand among the New England Patriots’ nine questionable to face the Detroit Lions in Germany. Both logged back-to-back limited practices at the FC Bayern Munich training ground while working back from knee injuries. Fullback Reggie Gilliam, tight end Cameron Latu, offensive linemen Walter Rouse and Greg Van Roten, cornerback Charles Woods, and safeties Kevin Byard III and Brenden Schoolers also carry game designations for head coach Mike Vrabel’s side of the aisle. Here’s the final injury report ahead of Sunday’s 9:30 a.m. ET kickoff at Allianz Arena. OUT Patriots RB TreVeyon Henderson (illness — out) G Ben Brown (knee — out) CB Carlton Davis III (knee — out) Lions C Cade Mays (ankle) CB D.J. Reed (hip) S Kerby Joseph (knee — PUP return) The Patriots ruled out three prior to the overseas flight. Henderson will be missing his third consecutive game in the backfield due to an illness . In addition to the No. 38 overall pick in the 2025 NFL draft, New England will also go without starters at left guard and cornerback due to knee injuries that arose during last weekend’s 45-27 blowout loss to the Green Bay Packers at Gillette Stadium. As for head coach Dan Campbell’s contingent, the Lions also previously ruled out three. item.title: 'I knew girls' wrestling would explode' says Skylar Grote
item.description: Skylar Grote knows all about the challenges young girls face in the sport of wrestling. That's because she’s been in their wrestling shoes. One of the Garden State's pioneers in female wrestling, Grote talked about her experiences on and off the mat during a presentation to present and future grapplers at Audubon High School on Thursday. “There’s been a lot of opportunities for these young girls in the sport lately and those are only increasing,” said Grote, who was the 2022 U.S. Open and Senior Pan American champion and placed fifth at the U.S. Olympic Trails in 2024. “I knew wrestling would explode at some point for girls. It’s cool to see a sport that teaches you so much being offered for both genders now.” Grote, the youngest of seven siblings, was introduced to wrestling at an early age and started competing when she was eight years old. Her father, Dr. Walter Grote, was a standout at Cornell University and was an alternate for the United States freestyle team in the 1976 Olympic Games. The Scotch Plains High School graduate was inducted into the New Jersey Chapter of the National Wrestling Hall of Fame in in 2023. Skylar Grote quickly learned that some of her toughest opponents in wrestling weren’t just the one across from her on the mat, but the people who felt that she shouldn’t be in a singlet and competing. She was the only girl on her elementary school team and, later, the only female on the vaunted Blair Academy wrestling team. “It was really hard at first,” Grote, now 28, said. “There were adults who against me and even some of my own teammates were against me.” Audubon junior Peyton Brining can relate to being the only female wrestler on a boys’ team. It wasn’t long ago that the Green Wave star was in a similar situation. “It was nice to hear someone who is a really good role model talk about a not-so-great experience about being the only girl on an all-boys team and how she turned it into a positive experience,” said Brining, who placed fifth in the state last winter. Girls’ wrestling has exploded in New Jersey since becoming an official sport in the 2018-19 season. Fewer than 500 girls competed in the inaugural season; that number has grown to nearly 3,000 according to data from the National Federation of High Schools. At Audubon, girls’ head coach Bill Scully said he’s expecting eight or nine wrestlers to compete this season, up from three last winter, and there’s plenty of interest in the middle school program, too. Grote explained how her outlook in wrestling, and in life, changed when she stopped listening to negative voices – including the one in her own mind. “For a large majority of my life, there was a negative voice in my head,” Grote said. “Changing that voice and becoming more positive has drastically changed the quality of my life. “Also being able to manage my emotions without taking on everyone else’s was important, too. Let go of those things you can’t control.” Grote has maintained her Jersey girl roots. She is an

One of the Garden State's pioneers in female wrestling, Grote talked about her experiences on and off the mat during a presentation to present and future grapplers at Audubon High School on Thursday. “There’s been a lot of opportunities for these young girls in the sport lately and those are only increasing,” said Grote, who was the 2022 U.S. Open and Senior Pan American champion and placed fifth at the U.S. Olympic Trails in 2024. “I knew wrestling would explode at some point for girls. She is an instructor at the Iron Horse Wrestling Club and was a commentator on the broadcast of last year’s state championships in Atlantic City. item.title: San Joaquin County girls volleyball CIF State quarterfinal scores, recap
item.description: The first round couldn't have gone much better. All four San Joaquin County girls volleyball teams won their CIF State playoff openers Tuesday, Nov. 10 . Two days later, the road got tougher . Only two of those four teams survived the quarterfinals Thursday, Nov. 12, keeping their state championship hopes alive. Here's how each team fared, along with the scores and a full recap. Division II No. 1 St. Mary's 3, No. 8 Harbor 2 The lower the division number, the tougher the competition and the less separation there seems to be between seeds. St. Mary's is finding that out the hard way. Two days after being pushed to five sets by No. 16 Cardinal Newman , the top-seeded Rams needed another comeback to defeat No. 8 Harbor, the Santa Cruz Coast Athletic League champion and Central Coast Section Division III title winner. St. Mary's dropped the first and third sets before rallying for a 21-25, 25-18, 20-25, 25-16, 15-12 victory . According to MaxPreps, the Rams are ranked No. 73 in California, while Harbor sits just seven spots behind at No. 80. For a closer look at how St. Mary's survived, read The Record's full game story. Division III No. 3 Ripon 3, No. 6 Bullard 0 It's hard to believe a program could reach four straight CIF Sac-Joaquin Section championship games, win two of them and advance to the state tournament each year without winning a single state playoff match. Yet that was Ripon's reality over the previous four seasons. After the Indians fell in this year's CIF Sac-Joaquin Section Division III championship , coach Gregory Soliz encouraged his players to turn that disappointment into something more. "Not a lot of teams can get to this point, and they did. At the same time, they're not happy about it I told them, let it hurt. Embrace the hurt. Then get ready for state." Apparently, his message got through. Ripon secured its second straight state tournament victory with a 25-15, 25-14, 25-15 sweep of Bullard, the County/Metro League runner-up. Setter Alayna Sprinkle recorded 31 assists and three kills, opposite and right-side hitter Jorie Eskes finished with 12 kills, and outside hitter Lilia Tuputala added 11. Outside hitter Ashlyn Malone made her presence felt with 10 kills, 11 digs and seven aces. Division IV No. 3 Santa Cruz 3, No. 6 Ripon Christian 1 If there was ever a reminder of how slim the margins can be in the state tournament, Ripon Christian's nearly 100-mile trip to Santa Cruz provided one. The Knights took the opening set 25-23 against the Santa Cruz Coast League and Central Coast Section Division III runner-up, only to drop the next two by identical 25-23 scores before falling 25-18 in the fourth. Santa Cruz entered ranked No. 177 in California by MaxPreps compared with Ripon Christian at No. 337, but the Knights made the matchup much closer than those rankings suggested. item.title: Kevin De Bruyne hails ‘amazing’ Real Madrid star: ‘We based our game plan around him’
item.description: Kevin De Bruyne hails ‘amazing’ Real Madrid star: ‘We based our game plan around him’ Napoli and Belgium star Kevin De Bruyne has this week moved to reveal his appreciation for the talents of Real Madrid starlet Arda Güler. This comes fresh off the pair locking horns on the international front, in a Nations League clash between Türkiye and Belgium. When all was said and done on the evening, it was the latter who secured all three points, courtesy of a comeback 2-1 triumph at The Gürsel Aksel Stadium. But it was youngster Arda who, in defeat, proved himself the star of the show. Continuing what has been a spectacular opening to the new campaign, the 21-year-old took the game by the scruff of the neck, proving himself Türkiye’s leading source of inspiration, and netting a stunning free-kick to open the scoring. Speaking to the media post-match, Kevin De Bruyne was therefore drawn on the name of his fellow midfielder. And the 35-year-old made use of the opportunity to absolutely lavish praise on Arda: ”Arda Güler is amazing. I think his teammates should take more responsibility because all of the responsibility is on him. They should help him. ”We based our plan on Arda. He is one of the best players in the world.” Conor Laird – GSFN

item.title: Eight sentenced to jail over Nurmagomedov-Dvalishvili brawl
item.description: Merab Dvalishvili (left) has won 21 of his 27 professional fights [Getty Images] Eight people have received prison sentences for their part in a mass brawl involving MMA fighters Usman Nurmagomedov and Merab Dvalishvili at a hotel in Abu Dhabi on Wednesday. A video of the incident appeared to show Russian Nurmagomedov slapping former UFC bantamweight champion Dvalishvili after approaching the Georgian from behind. Fighting then broke out between the two and members of their teams, with Abu Dhabi police later confirming the incident led to 10 arrests being made. According to a social media post by Abu Dhabi's judicial department, all 10 defendants have been convicted for their part in the brawl. A report by Abu Dhabi news outlet the National went into more detail, adding that six of the defendants were sentenced to six months in prison, fined £62,000 each and ordered to be deported after completing their sentences. It added they have been convicted for "disturbing public security, causing panic and endangering lives". Two others were given the same punishment, but for "violating privacy by using information technology to film and publish footage of the brawl". The remaining two defendants were fined £10,200 each for "disturbing public security and assaulting others". None of the defendants have yet been named, but Real American Freestyle (RAF) co-founder Chad Bronstein says Dvalishvili has been released from custody. "I'm pleased to share that Merab Dvalishvili is back with us in Abu Dhabi," Bronstein said in a statement. "We would like to express our sincere appreciation to the relevant authorities in Abu Dhabi for their professionalism and support. "We remain focused on moving forward and are pleased to have Merab back with us." BBC Sport has asked Abu Dhabi's judicial department for confirmation. Dvalishvili, 35, was scheduled to compete at the RAF event in the United Arab Emirates on Saturday against Brazilian Marlon Moraes. Dvalishvili released a video after the incident calling Nurmagomedov, 28, and his team "snakes" as he received treatment on his bloodied face. Nurmagomedov is in Abu Dhabi to support his brother Umar, who was set to compete against American Urijah Faber at Saturday's event. Nurmagomedov and Dvalishvili's teams had a previous altercation at a RAF event in July, which UFC champion Islam Makhachev - a close friend and training partner of the Nurmagomedovs - suggested led to Wednesday's brawl. Nurmagomedov is the PFL lightweight champion but is out of contract after winning his last bout with the organisation in July. He has been heavily linked with a switch to the UFC but on Friday the promotion's president Dana White said he had not spoken to the Russian. White then called the altercation "ridiculous" and "stupid", and referred to the participants as "a bunch of idiots". item.content:encoded: Merab Dvalishvili (left) has won 21 of his 27 professional fights [Getty Images] Eight people have received prison sentences for their part in a mass brawl involving MMA fighters Usman Nurmagomedov and Merab Dvalishvili at a hotel in Abu Dhabi on Wednesday. A video of the incident appeared to show Russian Nurmagomedov slapping former UFC bantamweight champion Dvalishvili after approaching the Georgian from behind. Fighting then broke out between the two and members of their teams, with Abu Dhabi police later confirming the incident led to 10 arrests being made. According to a social media post by Abu Dhabi's judicial department, all 10 defendants have been convicted for their part in the brawl. A report by Abu Dhabi news outlet the National went into more detail, adding that six of the defendants were sentenced to six months in prison, fined £62,000 each and ordered to be deported after completing their sentences. It added they have been convicted for "disturbing public security, causing panic and endangering lives". Two others were given the same punishment, but for "violating privacy by using information technology to film and publish footage of the brawl". The remaining two defendants were fined £10,200 each for "disturbing public security and assaulting others". None of the defendants have yet been named, but Real American Freestyle (RAF) co-founder Chad Bronstein says Dvalishvili has been released from custody. "I'm pleased to share that Merab Dvalishvili is back with us in Abu Dhabi," Bronstein said in a statement. "We would like to express our sincere appreciation to the relevant authorities in Abu Dhabi for their professionalism and support. "We remain focused on moving forward and are pleased to have Merab back with us." BBC Sport has asked Abu Dhabi's judicial department for confirmation. Dvalishvili, 35, was scheduled to compete at the RAF event in the United Arab Emirates on Saturday against Brazilian Marlon Moraes. Dvalishvili released a video after the incident calling Nurmagomedov, 28, and his team "snakes" as he received treatment on his bloodied face. Nurmagomedov is in Abu Dhabi to support his brother Umar, who was set to compete against American Urijah Faber at Saturday's event. Nurmagomedov and Dvalishvili's teams had a previous altercation at a RAF event in July, which UFC champion Islam Makhachev - a close friend and training partner of the Nurmagomedovs - suggested led to Wednesday's brawl. Nurmagomedov is the PFL lightweight champion but is out of contract after winning his last bout with the organisation in July. He has been heavily linked with a switch to the UFC but on Friday the promotion's president Dana White said he had not spoken to the Russian. White then called the altercation "ridiculous" and "stupid", and referred to the participants as "a bunch of idiots". item.title: Is Jalen Suggs playing tonight? Magic vs. Bucks injury report
item.description: Mike Watters-Imagn Images Is Jalen Suggs playing tonight? Magic vs. Bucks injury report appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Orlando Magic could receive a significant boost ahead of Friday night’s NBA Cup matchup against the Milwaukee Bucks, as guard Jalen Suggs has been upgraded to questionable with a right knee contusion and bone bruise. Orlando’s latest injury report Friday morning listed the 25-year-old as questionable, signaling a potential return after missing the team’s previous eight games. The Magic (4-7) will host the struggling Bucks (1-11) at the Kia Center, with tipoff scheduled for 7 p.m. ET. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Suggs last appeared in Orlando’s 111-102 victory over the New York Knicks on Oct. 25. He finished with four points, six rebounds, six assists and three steals across 34 minutes, shooting 2-for-8 from the field and 0-for-3 from beyond the arc. Through three appearances this season, Suggs is averaging eight points, 5.7 assists, five rebounds and two steals while shooting 35.7% from the field and 11.1% from 3-point range in 33.3 minutes per game. His potential return would provide additional backcourt depth for first-year head coach Sean Sweeney, whose team has struggled with injuries throughout the opening weeks of the 2026-27 campaign. Orlando enters Friday riding a two-game winning streak following Wednesday’s 123-108 victory over the Utah Jazz , which concluded its four-game road trip. Jalen Suggs’ potential return could provide crucial boost for injury-riddled Magic Despite the encouraging update on Suggs, Orlando continues to deal with several notable injuries. Star forward Paolo Banchero remains out with a right high ankle sprain, which has sidelined him since the team’s Oct. 23 loss to the Minnesota Timberwolves. Forward Tristan da Silva is questionable with a left calf strain, while Jamal Cain is also questionable because of a left shoulder contusion. Meanwhile, Jonathan Isaac remains out due to left knee injury management, and Izaiyah Nelson continues recovering from a left ankle injury. Second-year forward Noah Penda is also unavailable with a partially torn right hamstring. With Orlando looking to extend its winning streak to three games, Suggs’ availability could provide a timely boost against Milwaukee. However, his questionable designation does not guarantee that he will play Friday night. The Magic will determine his final status closer to tipoff. Related: Moe Wagner has joking reaction to heated altercation with former Magic coach Jamahl Mosley Related: Magic rumors: Orlando pushing back on rising trade buzz, but something’s gotta give soon

item.title: Tare: ‘Milan biggest disappointment was Pulisic, choosing Allegri, Cardinale problem’
item.description: Tare: ‘Milan biggest disappointment was Pulisic, choosing Allegri, Cardinale problem’ Milan sacked Igli Tare in May, but he has broken his silence on why he chose Max Allegri, not getting the chance to speak to owner Gerry Cardinale, and why ‘Christian Pulisic was the biggest disappointment.’ The former Lazio chief was brought in as director of sport, a role that until his arrival had not existed at the club for a while, since the dismissal of Paolo Maldini and Ricky Massara in 2023. He did not even last a full year, as Tare was sacked along with coach Allegri, CEO Giorgio Furlani and director Geoffrey Moncada with a single, brutal press statement on May 25. Tare spills beans on Milan experience VERONA, ITALY – APRIL 19: Igli Tare, Sporting Director of AC Milan looks on prior to the Serie A match between Hellas Verona FC and AC Milan at Stadio Marcantonio Bentegodi on April 19, 2026 in Verona, Italy. (Photo by Alessandro Sabattini/Getty Images) “The wound of failing to qualify for the Champions League is still deep, enormous in fact,” Tare told Sky Sport Italia Calcio Unplugged. “If I come to a club like Milan with the target of getting into the Champions League, then I don’t know where I am. This is the most successful club in Italian football history, and after Real Madrid it is the most important in the world.” RedBird patron Cardinale had been an aloof figure at first, but decided after cleaning house that he would take a much more hands-on approach to running the club. “I am disappointed that those leading the club didn’t understand people needed to be given time, something that they are now doing better,” added Tare. PISA, ITALY – FEBRUARY 13: Igli Tare of AC Milan looks on during the Serie A match between Pisa SC and AC Milan at Arena Garibaldi on February 13, 2026 in Pisa, Italy. (Photo by Gabriele Maltinti/Getty Images) “I’d say you need several transfer market sessions to get a team that is competitive and ready to win. At the start, there was an important responsibility, missing out on Europe altogether and losing the Coppa Italia Final did a lot of damage to morale. “We sold players for a lot of money and signed 10 new figures, so it takes time to integrate, understand and create a united group. We had, albeit in difficult circumstances, been first or second up until the end of March and start of April. In the last 10 rounds, our mentality just collapsed due to other issues that I don’t want to get into, but they did have an effect. “I admit we too deserve some of the blame, because Max and I should’ve paid more attention to certain dynamics, be more present with the squad to get the season over the line.” UDINE, ITALY – SEPTEMBER 20: Igli Tare, Sporting director of AC Milan looks on prior to the Serie A match between Udinese Calcio and AC Milan at Stadio Friuli on September 20, 2025 in Udine, Italy. (Photo by Emmanuele Ciancaglini/Getty Images) When Tare was brought in, it was meant to be as a director of sport, but he insists he nev
item.content:encoded: Tare: ‘Milan biggest disappointment was Pulisic, choosing Allegri, Cardinale problem’ Milan sacked Igli Tare in May, but he has broken his silence on why he chose Max Allegri, not getting the chance to speak to owner Gerry Cardinale, and why ‘Christian Pulisic was the biggest disappointment.’ The former Lazio chief was brought in as director of sport, a role that until his arrival had not existed at the club for a while, since the dismissal of Paolo Maldini and Ricky Massara in 2023. He did not even last a full year, as Tare was sacked along with coach Allegri, CEO Giorgio Furlani and director Geoffrey Moncada with a single, brutal press statement on May 25. Tare spills beans on Milan experience VERONA, ITALY – APRIL 19: Igli Tare, Sporting Director of AC Milan looks on prior to the Serie A match between Hellas Verona FC and AC Milan at Stadio Marcantonio Bentegodi on April 19, 2026 in Verona, Italy. (Photo by Alessandro Sabattini/Getty Images) “The wound of failing to qualify for the Champions League is still deep, enormous in fact,” Tare told Sky Sport Italia Calcio Unplugged. “If I come to a club like Milan with the target of getting into the Champions League, then I don’t know where I am. This is the most successful club in Italian football history, and after Real Madrid it is the most important in the world.” RedBird patron Cardinale had been an aloof figure at first, but decided after cleaning house that he would take a much more hands-on approach to running the club. “I am disappointed that those leading the club didn’t understand people needed to be given time, something that they are now doing better,” added Tare. PISA, ITALY – FEBRUARY 13: Igli Tare of AC Milan looks on during the Serie A match between Pisa SC and AC Milan at Arena Garibaldi on February 13, 2026 in Pisa, Italy. (Photo by Gabriele Maltinti/Getty Images) “I’d say you need several transfer market sessions to get a team that is competitive and ready to win. At the start, there was an important responsibility, missing out on Europe altogether and losing the Coppa Italia Final did a lot of damage to morale. “We sold players for a lot of money and signed 10 new figures, so it takes time to integrate, understand and create a united group. We had, albeit in difficult circumstances, been first or second up until the end of March and start of April. In the last 10 rounds, our mentality just collapsed due to other issues that I don’t want to get into, but they did have an effect. “I admit we too deserve some of the blame, because Max and I should’ve paid more attention to certain dynamics, be more present with the squad to get the season over the line.” UDINE, ITALY – SEPTEMBER 20: Igli Tare, Sporting director of AC Milan looks on prior to the Serie A match between Udinese Calcio and AC Milan at Stadio Friuli on September 20, 2025 in Udine, Italy. (Photo by Emmanuele Ciancaglini/Getty Images) When Tare was brought in, it was meant to be as a director of sport, but he insists he never had a direct line to the man with the purse strings. “I remember when we were in negotiations for Ardon Jashari, he called and wanted to understand what was happening. He said ‘if you need to spend a little more, just let me know, and I’m ready.’ However, I never got the chance to speak with him directly again, because there were people above me I didn’t want to over-ride. “It would’ve been helpful to everyone, not just me, if we’d been able to discuss it directly. I think this is a new experience for Cardinale, he is used to other sports in America, but now he has taken on the responsibility at Milan. “I would’ve preferred to have that presence when I was still at Milan, as it would’ve been very useful, but better late than never for the good of the club. I think the good of Milan is top of his priorities too.” MILAN, ITALY – APRIL 26: Luka Modric of AC Milan is consoled by Massimiliano Allegri, Head Coach of AC Milan, as he is assisted off by medical staff after going down injured during the Serie A match between AC Milan and Juventus FC at Giuseppe Meazza Stadium on April 26, 2026 in Milan, Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) Among the roles tasked to Tare was the choice of a new coach, and he plumped for Allegri. “I was thinking of the experience he brought at that time. When I arrived, the only thing I was asked was to hire an Italian coach, not a foreign one,” revealed Tare. “I had a few ideas for foreign coaches, but the experience with Sergio Conceicao and Paulo Fonseca evidently wasn’t what they were after. Allegri won a lot as a coach, Milan is special to him, he won the Scudetto there first, so of course he was sad at the way it ended. “He is not alone, Zlatan Ibrahimovic and Alessandro Nesta had great experiences elsewhere too, but Milan stands out for them, and I can confirm it’s true.” SALZBURG, AUSTRIA – OCTOBER 15: Luka Modric of AC Milan looks on before the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD2 match between FC Salzburg and AC Milan at Stadion Salzburg on October 15, 2026 in Salzburg, Austria. (Photo by Jasmin Walter/Getty Images) This is also a legendary club abroad, and it is what prompted the arrival of Ballon d’Or winner Luka Modric as a free agent after the experience at Real Madrid. “I had the sensation this squad lacked leadership. The idea along with Modric was to sign Granit Xhaka, who at the time was the captain of Bayer Leverkusen, to guide the others. Luka is more silent in his attitude on the pitch.” There was an intriguing comment from Tare that suggested more tension behind the scenes with some players. “The biggest disappointment was Pulisic, I expected more from him in terms of responsibility and leadership. He’s a great player, but some things happened that I had never experienced in my career. Pulisic didn’t score a goal for six months. Santiago Gimenez didn’t score either. “I guess these things happen in football, but when you have a drought that long, it ends up affecting the whole team’s performance.”

item.title: New Rumor Offers NY Yankees Fantastic Upgrade Option at 3B, But It Comes With a BIG Risk
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect With the New York Yankees in search of an upgrade at third base, a two-time All-Star in his prime could be had at a reasonable price. But a potential trade comes with a big risk. Despite winning 93 games while being in the same division as the American League Champion Tampa Bay Rays , the Yankees had some obvious weaknesses this season. Second baseman Jazz Chisholm Jr. frustrated fans during a down year. Third baseman Ryan McMahon continued to disappoint at the plate after being acquired before the 2025 trade deadline. And homegrown product Austin Wells was an automatic out all season. Replacing Wells is unlikely this offseason, and either Anthony Volpe or Luis Garcia Jr. is likely to take over at 2B in 2027. However, third base is a position the Yankees are working hard to upgrade after general manager Brian Cashman said it is “without a doubt” a top priority at this week’s GM meeting in Las Vegas. Unfortunately, the free agent market isn’t overflowing with great options. Philadelphia Phillies veteran Alec Bohm is reportedly on the club’s wish list, but according to FanSided’s Robert Murray, “ one name that I hear is popular is Phillies free agent Alec Bohm .” So the Yankees might have to engage in an unfavorable bidding war for the one-time All-Star. Could the New York Yankees make Isaac Paredes trade for a reasonable price? Sep 26, 2026; West Sacramento, California, USA; Houston Astros third baseman Isaac Paredes (15) warms up before the game against the Athletics at Sutter Health Park. Mandatory Credit: Dennis Lee-Imagn Images That is why the trade market could be Cashman’s route to improve the hot corner. Houston Astros star Isaac Paredes would be a great addition for New York this offseason, and according to ESPN’s Alden Gonzalez, he could be acquired at a more reasonable rate than Yankees fans might have thought. In a new report, the MLB insider noted that the Astros have a roster construction problem and moving either Christian Walker, Paredes, or Jeremy Pena could help fix the problem. However, with all three only having one season left on their deals, sources claim moving them is “really difficult” because teams are having trouble justifying a trade with “uncertainty of how many games — if any — will be played in 2027.” It is good news for the Yankees if they are willing to take the risk. Paredes is a far better hitter than McMahon — he posted a .262 AVG, .806 OPS, 25 home runs, and 96 RBIs last season — and is a versatile infielder who can play first, second, and third base. If other teams are wary of a trade before a lockout, it could drive down the price and limit the competitors. However, the possibility of lost games or an entire lost season is a good reason to be hesitant about giving up assets for a player they won’t get a full season out of. item.title: MLB rumors: Athletics’ trade candidate will catch Yankees’ attention
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Sergio Estrada-Imagn Images MLB rumors: Athletics’ trade candidate will catch Yankees’ attention appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The New York Yankees were linked to catchers ahead of the 2026 MLB trade deadline. One has to imagine they may consider a catcher trade pursuit this offseason. All-Star Shea Langeliers of the Athletics is reportedly a candidate to be moved ahead of the 2027 campaign, and the Yankees could be a fit. “The Athletics’ Shea Langeliers (controllable through 2028) is another trade possibility,” MLB.com reported recently . “… A torn meniscus in his right knee ended any chance he had of being moved before the Deadline, but the Athletics could consider dangling him this winter as they look for ways to improve their pitching staff.” As mentioned, Langeliers suffered an injury before the trade deadline which led to the possibility of a deal occurring at the time drastically decreasing. Things are different now, however. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The 28-year-old still has a couple years of team control remaining on his contract. The Athletics need pitching, and moving Langeliers could help them address that area of their roster. Langeliers’ trade value remains high despite his previous injury concern. In 2026, he earned the first All-Star selection of his big league career and ultimately hit .262 with an .802 OPS and 23 home runs. Although he wasn’t an All-Star in 2025, the backstop hit .277 with 31 home runs and an .861 OPS. He had 29 long balls in 2024 as well, so his track record proves his consistency in the power department. It remains to be seen if the Yankees officially have interest in a potential Shea Langeliers trade this offseason. At the very least, the fit makes sense. Related: MLB rumors: There’s a lot of buzz around Mariners stealing major Cubs free agent Related: MLB rumors: Tigers linked to major Cubs free agent pitcher

item.title: Warriors superstar has wild rehab plan — and says he’ll fistfight GM to make it happen
item.description: Both members of the Golden State Warriors’ superstar backcourt duo are injured. Steph Curry is expected to miss at least several weeks after suffering an oblique abdominal tear during Wednesday’s game. Jimmy Butler continues to work his way back to the court after tearing his ACL last season, and should be able to play in January or February. Jimmy Butler III #10 and Stephen Curry #30 of the Golden State Warriors look on during a game against the New Orleans Pelicans, Nov. 9, 2026, in San Francisco. NBAE via Getty Images When Butler is able to return, Golden State will have to choose whether they want him to play rehab games with their G League affiliate, the Santa Cruz Warriors, or return straight to Golden State. Although Butler seems to have already made his decision. “I’m going down to Santa Cruz to hoop. It may not be for long, but I’m going to play in Santa Cruz. I’m playing in a f****** game,” Butler told The Athletic. “I’m definitely coming down there to play. So good luck to everybody. Y’all ain’t gonna get too many minutes out of me, but I’m definitely going down there. I want to hoop,” he added. Jimmy Butler III of the Golden State Warriors arrives at Chase Center before a game against the New Orleans Pelicans in San Francisco on Nov. 9, 2026. NBAE via Getty Images Golden State Warriors General Manager Mike Dunleavy Jr. speaks at a media day press conference at Chase Center in San Francisco, California, Sept. 28, 2026. Getty Images Butler was then asked whether he got his desire to play in Santa Cruz cleared with Mike Dunleavy Jr., the Warriors’ GM . “I don’t got to clear s*** with nobody. I’m going. Me and Mike will fistfight. He’s gonna be like, ‘Jimmy, no.’ I’m gonna be like, ‘Mike, yes. I’m going to G League, baby!’ Y’all know where to find me. Santa Cruz, baby,” Butler responded. Butler was clearly just kidding. Plus, he and Dunleavy Jr. were teammates on the Chicago Bulls for three seasons, so they don’t have a typical player-front office executive relationship. Threat of violence aside, Dunleavy Jr. will probably appreciate how eager Butler is to return.

item.title: Brett Yormark has a new home in Milan
item.description: Big 12 Commissioner Brett Yormark speaks at a press conference during the 2026 Phillips 66 Big 12 Men's Basketball Tournament at the T-Mobile Center in Kansas City, Mo., on Tuesday, March 10, 2026. | Rio Giancarlo, Deseret News Brett Yormark’s next move is taking him well outside the Big 12 footprint. The outgoing Big 12 commissioner is heading to Milan, Italy, where he has been named chief executive of Milan Sports & Entertainment, a newly launched holding company backed by RedBird Capital Partners , the investment firm behind Italian soccer powerhouse AC Milan. Yormark’s new job will be about much more than soccer. MSE will bring together RedBird’s investments in sports, business and live entertainment in Milan, with Yormark overseeing the company’s business strategy and efforts to expand its presence internationally. “It’s an honor and a privilege to take on this role in a city with Milan’s history and passion for sport,” Yormark said in the announcement . “I understand the responsibility that comes with leading an organization connected to institutions that mean so much to their supporters and communities. Throughout my career, I have helped sports organizations evolve, expand their reach and create new opportunities, and I look forward to drawing on that experience to execute RedBird’s vision for MSE.” One of the biggest projects on his plate will be the development of a new 71,500-seat stadium for AC Milan and city rival Inter Milan. The two clubs are working together on the venue, which will replace the historic San Siro stadium. But RedBird has bigger ambitions for the city. Big 12 Commissioner Brett Yormark speaks at a press conference during the 2026 Phillips 66 Big 12 Men's Basketball Tournament at the T-Mobile Center in Kansas City, Mo., on Tuesday, March 10, 2026. | Rio Giancarlo, Deseret News The company also plans to explore building a venue-management business focused on food and beverage, merchandise and premium hospitality. It is also evaluating the possibility of acquiring a Milan franchise in the proposed NBA Europe league , developing another sports and entertainment venue in nearby San Donato Milanese and expanding the city’s presence in international tennis. Yormark will report directly to RedBird founder and managing partner Gerry Cardinale. His new role is expected to begin after his departure from the Big 12. That departure was announced at the end of October, bringing an end to a four-year run as commissioner of the conference. Yormark, who took over in 2022, oversaw the additions of eight schools, including BYU and Utah, while helping guide the league through major changes in college athletics. BYU had been invited to join the league just before Yormark assumed his position. Sources: Big 12 Commissioner Brett Yormark is leaving the conference. Yormark made the decision to leave and is expected to accept a new role outside of college sports in the near future. He’ll be with the league at least through January of 2027. p

The two clubs are working together on the venue, which will replace the historic San Siro stadium. But RedBird has bigger ambitions for the city. Big 12 Commissioner Brett Yormark speaks at a press conference during the 2026 Phillips 66 Big 12 Men's Basketball Tournament at the T-Mobile Center in Kansas City, Mo., on Tuesday, March 10, 2026. | Rio Giancarlo, Deseret News The company also plans to explore building a venue-management business focused on food and beverage, merchandise and premium hospitality. It is also evaluating the possibility of acquiring a Milan franchise in the proposed NBA Europe league , developing another sports and entertainment venue in nearby San Donato Milanese and expanding the city’s presence in international tennis. That departure was announced at the end of October, bringing an end to a four-year run as commissioner of the conference. Yormark, who took over in 2022, oversaw the additions of eight schools, including BYU and Utah, while helping guide the league through major changes in college athletics. BYU had been invited to join the league just before Yormark assumed his position. Sources: Big 12 Commissioner Brett Yormark is leaving the conference. Yormark made the decision to leave and is expected to accept a new role outside of college sports in the near future. He’ll be with the league at least through January of 2027. pic.twitter.com/M0XnkCIPfe — Pete Thamel (@PeteThamel) October 30, 2026 Under his leadership, the Big 12 secured its latest media rights agreement, which pays member schools more than $30 million annually. The conference also saw significant growth in sponsorship and partnership revenue. Yormark is expected to remain with the Big 12 through the end of January, giving the conference time to find its next commissioner. Now, after spending the last several years navigating the changing landscape of college athletics, Yormark is preparing for a new challenge: helping build Milan into an even bigger international sports and entertainment destination.

item.title: Branding it like Beckham: how Jude Bellingham is future-proofing his fame
item.description: From Calvin Klein to British Vogue, the Real Madrid man is leading the way when it comes to football’s foray into fashion. But is he playing it safe? This Sunday, Jude Bellingham will line up with his England teammates for a match against Spain. But the footballer has been hitting the headlines way beyond the pitch recently – thanks to fronting a Calvin Klein underwear ad released this month, and becoming the first footballer to appear solo on the cover of British Vogue . It’s a savvy move for the 23-year-old, future-proofing himself as a power player both on and off the pitch. This is a roadmap carved out by David Beckham, who since retiring in 2013 has become a brand and personality that transcends sport. Beckham – together with his wife, Victoria – became a billionaire this year. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Taking a brief minute to remember Pierre Sage’s impact at Crystal Palace
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! So farewell then, Pierre Sage . Many coaches leave under a cloud, not many have their departures completely obscured by the foul, retch-inducing one emanating from another team’s managerial circus, but such was Sage’s fate . The news section of Crystal Palace’s website helpfully tells you the amount of time it might take you to read each story it links through to. For example it should take four minutes or so to get through Tuesday’s “On this day: five big Crystal Palace birthdays”. “England: I love a knee slide!” will take you five. “Prize draw: be a mascot for our next [Bigger Vase] tie!” is a two-minute job. The statement informing the world of Sage’s exit? One minute. Eighty-three words. By way of illustration, the word “words” was the 84th of this paragraph. Just because the man’s French doesn’t mean his exit should be marked with a shrug. As I have been away at a conference, giving a presentation that the MC described as ‘sobering’, I’ve missed the last few days of football, so I was very sad to read about the passing of the great Danny Kelly . Others are far better placed to give tributes to the great man, but for younger generations who can’t comprehend the football cultural significance, Baker and Kelly represented the peak of football phone-ins. Before it became people ranting and raving about wanting the manager sacked as they’ve lost a few games or wanting the club to spend another few hundred million pounds on yet more players, it was about football supporters and supporting, from fans who actually went to games. Their peak was on BBC Radio in the 1990s, and there are too many examples of their greatness, but if I had to pick one, just one to illustrate it, it would, of course, be Gordon the Dundee United supporter and his bow tie . Rest in Peace, Danny Kelly. You gave us such joy” – Noble Francis. As they no longer seem to be ‘Dr Tottenham’, I was wondering if they had maybe passed the soubriquet on. I think the England cricket team has provided the answer (again)” – Andrew Parker. Impressive list of kiss-off press releases ( yesterday’s Football Daily ) but why was Ralf Rangnick omitted from the chronological list of post-Fergie managers? Is it because Football Daily valued him as little as Manchester United fans did?” – Mike Wilner. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: Why Chelsea and Manchester City’s WSL clash is not as season-defining as you think
item.description: Neither side have lost in the league yet but a more competitive division should take title race to the wire There was a time when the games between the top three – traditionally Chelsea, Manchester City and Arsenal – were title-deciders. Where every point taken off a title rival was key. Such was the gap in investment and quality between those teams and the rest of the Women’s Super League, it was extremely rare that points would be dropped to teams outside that elite clique. As the WSL has grown in investment, profile and size, that narrative has started to shift a little. The investment gap is still large from the top to the bottom of the league. But increased investment among the best of the rest and even among those teams further down the table, as well as an increase in high-quality coaches with the tactical and technical vision to get more from players, is having an impact. Continue reading...

item.title: The beautiful game: revived art prize gives football its creative due once more | Emma John
item.description: Football and the art world have long remained distant but the breadth of entries for this year’s award reveals a healthy revival It may be the Beautiful Game, but in its early decades football was a rare subject for artists. The Italian Futurist Umberto Boccioni whirled an athlete’s body into a vortex of movement in his 1913 painting Dynamism of a Soccer Player . You can see one of the earliest fine art depictions of a match – a smoggy, factory-adjactent scene called Any Wintry Afternoon in England – at the Manchester Art Gallery. If 1930s abstraction is more your thing, you can enjoy decoding the geometric shapes in Kazimir Malevich’s Painterly Realism of a Football Player – Color Masses in the 4th Dimension. I’m guessing the small green pea shape is a ball. These, in any case, were exceptions. In 1953 the Football Association launched an art prize, backed by the newly formed Arts Council: the winning works included Going To The Match by LS Lowry, with its crowds flocking to Bolton Wanderers’ then home ground, Burnden Park. An exhibition of the submissions, Football and The Fine Arts, toured the country and the FA secretary, Sir Stanley Rous, said he hoped it would finally break the barrier between those two worlds. Continue reading...

item.title: Pochettino’s Chelsea maelstrom the best yardstick for what lies ahead at United
item.description: Argentinian oversaw high-scoring games in his one Chelsea season and Opta predicts his Manchester United side will move upfield quicker than that team Among the 20 managers with more than 290 matches in the Premier League, only the five “ big beasts ” of Alex Ferguson, Arsène Wenger, José Mourinho, Jürgen Klopp and Pep Guardiola have better points-per-game averages than Mauricio Pochettino. He is an elite manager. Pochettino took over Southampton midway through their first season back in the top flight (2012-13) after the club spent seven years in the lower leagues. In his only full campaign, they finished eighth. He led Tottenham to second in 2016-17, third in the seasons either side, and reached the 2019 Champions League final . item.title: It’s Happy Harry Kane day as England’s finest seizes his moment in style | Barney Ronay
item.description: The Ballon d’Or validated the forward’s career and he extended his incredible record for England with yet another goal on his 126th appearance Happy Harry Kane day! And many happy Harry returns. There is a process in clinical psychology known as semantic satiation. Subjects are asked to repeat a word or phrase so many times that it loses any kind of meaning. Suddenly “daffodils” is just an absurd, empty set of sounds. So it was in the buildup to Harry Kane’s record-breaking 126th cap, at the end of Harry Kane Ballon d’Or fortnight, as Harry Kane’s England were led out by top scorer Harry Kane, climax to a week of Harry Kane tributes, Harry Kane montages, 26-page Harry Kane … wait. Where were we? This was that kind of occasion from start to finish, a night where you expected to look up from your desk mid-match to see Kane’s head looming helpfully over your shoulder, to enter the Wembley toilets at half-time and find him silently offering you a breath mint and a scented tissue. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | ‘The club would like to thank …’: Manchester United dust off the heartfelt exit message
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Tuesday 22 April 2014: “Manchester United has announced that David Moyes has left the club. The club would like to place on record its thanks for the hard work, honesty and integrity he brought to the role.” Oh no! Where will the USA! USA! USA! ever be able to find a manager who could lead us to the dizzying heights of yet another humiliating defeat in the round of 16? A completely empty safari shirt on a clothes hanger could do that. Now he’s leaving the national team to prioritise a club team, which is exactly what he criticised Christian Pulisic for doing a while back. A $10m dollar buyout from Manchester United is a way more appealing prospect than another World Cup cycle with this guy. Adios, Mauricio. I’d add gracias , but for what, exactly?” – Chi. If any Manchester United fans weren’t already feeling that their board had totally lost its moral compass, then might I suggest that in holding the board meeting to seal Michael Carrick’s fate in Monaco a new bar in tone-deafness has been set. Out of touch, no? Pas du tout . Bonne chance, Mauricio, you are going to need it fella. Meanwhile, let’s pencil in the next board meeting for six months’ time or so. Circus Circus in Las Vegas anyone? Might be too many clowns” – John Collins. With Lil Wayne doing his bit in the jungle, how long before we do actually see Don Pochettino playing a starring role in the Joel & Jim-hosted caper show I’m A Previously Respectable Manager … Get Me Out Of Here?” – Ken Muir. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: Michael Carrick was just the latest fall guy for Manchester United’s dysfunctional hierarchy | Jamie Jackson
item.description: Disastrous decisions and confused appointments have been a constant theme at Old Trafford since Sir Alex Ferguson’s retirement in 2013 For a window into the alarming dysfunction at Manchester United that Michael Carrick failed to manage and caused his sacking , consider the case of Eddie Howe, initially a favourite to succeed the 45-year-old before Mauricio Pochettino’s emergence as the chosen one. The former Newcastle manager had been Jason Wilcox’s choice to take over from Carrick. Howe was also the favoured candidate of Dan Ashworth, Wilcox’s predecessor as United’s director of football, to follow Erik ten Hag after the Dutchman’s sacking in October 2024. Except Wilcox disagreed and Sir Jim Ratcliffe went with Wilcox’s man, Ruben Amorim, and that December Ashworth departed only five months after joining. Continue reading...

item.title: ‘Pregnancy does not mean game over’: meet the footballers challenging the myths | Moving the Goalposts
item.description: Claire Emslie and Emma Kelly are among those taking advantage of new research and guidelines for pregnant players Claire Emslie wasn’t expecting to be able to run at 81% of her max speed at 32 weeks pregnant. Emslie, a Scotland international who also plays as a forward for Angel City FC , documented her journey through pregnancy and football training on social media and is part of a growing number of professional female footballers who are getting pregnant in their athletic prime and approaching motherhood with a fresh mindset. Rather than marking the end of a career (notably, Millie Bright announced her pregnancy in September, months after having retired), pregnancy can mark both a continuation and a renewal. Continue reading...

item.title: Less drama, more listening, but is Kozo Tashima the candidate to topple Infantino?
item.description: Japan FA honorary president is hoping a calmer approach that makes fewer unwelcome headlines for Fifa will be welcomed by football Not many remember Japan’s bid for the 2022 World Cup, when the country finished the race with only two of the final 22 votes. Kozo Tashima was involved then, and now the honorary president of the Japan Football Association is going it alone in the hope of ousting Gianni Infantino. The 68-year-old Tashima is an unlikely insurgent and an unlikely challenger to Infantino. He is, however, a familiar and respected figure in Asian and global football politics, and ready to take the Fifa presidency out of the headlines into a quieter era. Continue reading...
